Model (\ref{eqn:MMEFM}) has the main effects split into ``global'' and ``local'', apparently increasing the number of parameters and main effect series to estimate. \label{remark:reference_group}
The reference group in the global alignment can be chosen arbitrarily in principle. In numerical implementation, we choose the group with the largest projected-core norm, for instance the largest value of $\sum_{t=1}^T\left\|\widehat{\mathbf{Q}}_m'\widecheck{\mathbf{Y}}_{G,t}^{(m)}\widehat{\mathbf{J}}_m\right\|_F^2$ to improve numerical stability and to avoid using a group whose global common component is nearly degenerate as the reference. A more formal procedure for detecting whether a group contains nonzero global common factors is given in Section~\ref{subsec:detect_global_cm}.

\label{remark:E1}
    The orthogonality condition $\mathbf{Q}_{e,m}\mathbf{Q}_{e,n}'=\0$ or $\mathbf{J}_{e,m}\mathbf{J}_{e,n}'=\0$ for each $m\ne n$ in (E1) is imposed to ensure that the error matrices are uncorrelated across groups, as required by (IC2). However, this condition could be relaxed, in which case the model would be asymptotically identified. Such a relaxation would introduce additional terms into the cross-group error products and lead to more complicated proofs and convergence rates. We do not pursue the corresponding theoretical extension here, but in simulation in subsection~\ref{subsec: simulation}, this condition is not imposed.

body_md:
\label{corollary:simplified_main_effect_rates}
    Let Assumptions~(IC1), (IC2), (E1), (E2) and (S1) hold. Suppose that (ME1) and (ME2) hold with pervasive main effect factors, i.e., $\gamma_r=\gamma_c=\gamma_r^{(m)}=\gamma_c^{(m)}=1$ for all $m\in[M]$, and that all main effect memory parameters are less than $1/4$. Then, for each $m\in[M]$ and $t\in[T]$, 
    \begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.5em, itemsep=1pt, parsep=0pt, topsep=2pt]
        \item $\big\| \widehat{\mathbf{A}}_{1m}-\widecheck{\mathbf{A}}_{1m}\mathbf{H}_{A_1,m} \big\|_F^2=O_P\big(1/T\big)$, $\big\| \widehat{\mathbf{B}}_{1m}-\widecheck{\mathbf{B}}_{1m}\mathbf{H}_{B_1,m} \big\|_F^2=O_P\big(1/T\big)$.
        \item $\big\| \widehat{\mathbf{A}}_{2m}-\widecheck{\mathbf{A}}_{2m}\mathbf{H}_{A_2,m} \big\|_F^2=O_P\big(1/T+1/(p_mq_m^2)\big)$, $\big\| \widehat{\mathbf{B}}_{2m}-\widecheck{\mathbf{B}}_{2m}\mathbf{H}_{B_2,m} \big\|_F^2=O_P\big(1/T+1/(q_mp_m^2)\big)$.
        \item $1/p_m\big\| \widehat{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}_t^{(m)}-\mathbf{H}_{A_2,m}^{-1}\widecheck{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}_t^{(m)} \big\|^2=O_P\big(1/T+1/(p_mq_m)\big)$, $1/q_m\big\| \widehat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}_t^{(m)}-\mathbf{H}_{B_2,m}^{-1}\widecheck{\boldsymbol{\beta}}_t^{(m)} \big\|^2=O_P\big(1/T+1/(p_mq_m)\big)$.
        \item $\big\| \widehat{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}_t-\mathbf{H}_\alpha^{-1}\widecheck{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}_t \big\|^2=O_P\big(1/T+\max_{n\in[M]}1/(p_nq_n)\big)$, $\big\| \widehat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}_t-\mathbf{H}_\beta^{-1}\widecheck{\boldsymbol{\beta}}_t \big\|^2=O_P\big(1/T+\max_{n\in[M]}1/(p_nq_n)\big)$.
        \item $1/p_m\big\| \widetilde{\mathbf{A}}_{1m}-\widecheck{\widecheck{\mathbf{A}}}_{1m}\mathbf{H}_\alpha \big\|_F^2=O_P\big(1/T+1/q_m\max_{n\in[M]}1/(p_nq_n)\big)$, $1/q_m\big\| \widetilde{\mathbf{B}}_{1m}-\widecheck{\widecheck{\mathbf{B}}}_{1m}\mathbf{H}_\beta \big\|_F^2=O_P\big(1/T+1/p_m\max_{n\in[M]}1/(p_nq_n)\big)$.
    \end{itemize}

body_md:
\label{remark:bootstrap}
The circular-shift bootstrap in Algorithm~\ref{alg:bootstrap} is formulated under the assumption that the factor series have a single stationary segment. For data with known or unknown structural breaks, or more generally with multiple regimes, whole-sample circular shifting may mix observations from different regimes. A possible extension is to first divide the sample into regimes, either using known break points or estimated break points from change point detection methods, and then apply circular shifting within each regime.

title: Proof
body_md:
The grand mean $c_t^{(m)}$ (as defined in \eqref{eqn:combined_main_effects}) is identified when we pre- and post-multiply by $\1_{p_m}'$ and $\1_{q_m}$ respectively on both sides of model (\ref{eqn:MMEFM}) under (IC1). Then for $\{\mathbf{a}_t^{(m)}\}$ and $\{\mathbf{b}_t^{(m)}\}$ we can post-multiply by $\1_{q_m}$ and pre-multiply by $\1_{p_m}'$ on both sides of (\ref{eqn:MMEFM}) respectively. The remaining common component is then identified as well.

For global and local effects, since $c_t^{(m)} = \mu_t + \mu_t^{(m)}$ is identified, we have $\mu_t = M^{-1}\sum_{m=1}^M c_t^{(m)}$ using (IC2), and hence both $\{\mu_t\}$ and $\{\mu_t^{(m)}\}$ are identified. Next, we in fact identify the row and column main effects at group $m$ respectively as
\begin{align}\label{eqn:main_effects}
    \mathbf{a}_t^{(m)} = q_m^{-1}\mathbf{M}_{p_m}(\mathbf{Y}_t^{(m)} - \mathbf{E}_t^{(m)})\1_{q_m}, \;\;\; \mathbf{b}_t^{(m)} = p_m^{-1}\mathbf{M}_{q_m}(\mathbf{Y}_t^{(m)} - \mathbf{E}_t^{(m)})'\1_{p_m}.
\end{align}
Hence for $m\neq n$, using (\ref{eqn:combined_main_effects}) and (IC2), we have
\begin{align}
    \mathbf{A}_{1m}\mathbbm{E}\bigg(T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\boldsymbol{\alpha}_t^{\otimes 2}\bigg)\mathbf{A}_{1n}' &= \mathbbm{E}\bigg(T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\mathbf{a}_t^{(m)}\mathbf{a}_t^{(n)'}\bigg) \nonumber \\
    &= q_m^{-1}q_n^{-1}\mathbf{M}_{p_m}\mathbbm{E}\bigg\{T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T(\mathbf{Y}_t^{(m)} - \mathbf{E}_t^{(m)})\1_{q_m}\1_{q_n}'(\mathbf{Y}_t^{(n)} - \mathbf{E}_t^{(n)})'\bigg\}\mathbf{M}_{p_n} \nonumber \\
    &= T^{-1}q_m^{-1}q_n^{-1}\mathbf{M}_{p_m}\sum_{t=1}^T\mathbbm{E}\{\mathbf{Y}_t^{(m)}\1_{q_m}\1_{q_n}'\mathbf{Y}_t^{(n)'}\}\mathbf{M}_{p_n}, \label{eqn: Omega_population} \\
    \mathbf{B}_{1m}\mathbbm{E}\bigg(T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\boldsymbol{\beta}_t^{\otimes 2}\bigg)\mathbf{B}_{1n}' &= \mathbbm{E}\bigg(T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\mathbf{b}_t^{(m)}\mathbf{b}_t^{(n)'}\bigg) \nonumber \\ 
    &= p_m^{-1}p_n^{-1}\mathbf{M}_{q_m}\mathbbm{E}\bigg\{T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T(\mathbf{Y}_t^{(m)}-\mathbf{E}_t^{(m)})'\1_{p_m}\1_{p_n}'(\mathbf{Y}_t^{(n)} - \mathbf{E}_t^{(n)})\bigg\}\mathbf{M}_{q_n} \nonumber \\
    &= T^{-1}p_m^{-1}p_n^{-1}\mathbf{M}_{q_m}\sum_{t=1}^T\mathbbm{E}\{\mathbf{Y}_t^{(m)'}\1_{p_m}\1_{p_n}'\mathbf{Y}_t^{(n)}\}\mathbf{M}_{q_n}. \nonumber 
\end{align}
If we define 
\begin{align*}
    \boldsymbol{\Omega}_{A_1,m} &:= (M-1)^{-1}\sum_{n=1;n\neq m}^M \bigg\{T^{-1}q_m^{-1}q_n^{-1}\mathbf{M}_{p_m}\sum_{t=1}^T\mathbbm{E}\{\mathbf{Y}_t^{(m)}\1_{q_m}\1_{q_n}'\mathbf{Y}_t^{(n)'}\}\mathbf{M}_{p_n}\bigg\}^{\otimes 2}, \\ 
    \boldsymbol{\Omega}_{B_1,m} &:= (M-1)^{-1}\sum_{n=1;n\neq m}^M \bigg\{T^{-1}p_m^{-1}p_n^{-1}\mathbf{M}_{q_m}\sum_{t=1}^T\mathbbm{E}\{\mathbf{Y}_t^{(m)'}\1_{p_m}\1_{p_n}'\mathbf{Y}_t^{(n)}\}\mathbf{M}_{q_n}\bigg\}^{\otimes 2},
\end{align*}
then a version of $\mathbf{A}_{1m}$ (resp.\ $\mathbf{B}_{1m}$) can be identified as the first $r_1$ eigenvectors of $\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{A_1,m}$  (resp.\ first $\ell_1$ eigenvectors of $\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{B_1,m}$). 

As for $\mathbf{A}_{2m}$, since $\mathbf{A}_{1m}^\perp$ have orthonormal columns spanning the orthogonal complement of the column space of $\mathbf{A}_{1m}$, from \eqref{eqn:combined_main_effects}, we have
\[\mathbf{A}_{1m}^{\perp'}\mathbf{a}_t^{(m)} = \mathbf{A}_{1m}^{\perp'}\mathbf{A}_{2m}\boldsymbol{\alpha}_t^{(m)}.\]
Hence 
\[T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\mathbf{a}_t^{(m)}\mathbf{a}_t^{(m)'}\mathbf{A}_{1m}^\perp = \mathbf{A}_{1m}\bigg(T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\boldsymbol{\alpha}_t\boldsymbol{\alpha}_t^{(m)'}\bigg)\mathbf{A}_{2m}'\mathbf{A}_{1m}^\perp + \mathbf{A}_{2m}\bigg(T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\boldsymbol{\alpha}_t^{(m)}\boldsymbol{\alpha}_{t}^{(m)'}\bigg)\mathbf{A}_{2m}'\mathbf{A}_{1m}^\perp.\]
Hence (IC2) gives
\begin{align}
    \bigg\{T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T(\mathbf{a}_t^{(m)\otimes 2})\mathbf{A}_{1m}^\perp\bigg\}^{\otimes 2} = \mathbf{A}_{2m}\bigg\{T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T(\boldsymbol{\alpha}_t^{(m)\otimes 2})\mathbf{A}_{2m}'\mathbf{A}_{1m}^\perp\bigg\}^{\otimes 2}\mathbf{A}_{2m}'.
    \label{eqn:S_A2m}
\end{align}
Therefore, we can take the first $r_2^{(m)}$ eigenvectors of $\Big\{T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\mathbf{a}_t^{(m)\otimes 2}\mathbf{A}_{1m}^\perp\Big\}^{\otimes 2}$ as a version of $\mathbf{A}_{2m}$. Similarly, we can take the first $\ell_{2}^{(m)}$ eigenvectors of $\Big\{T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\mathbf{b}_t^{(m)\otimes 2}\mathbf{B}_{1m}^\perp\Big\}^{\otimes 2}$ as a version of $\mathbf{B}_{2m}$.





To identify $\boldsymbol{\alpha}_t^{(m)}$, since
$\mathbf{A}_{1m}^{\perp '}\mathbf{A}_{2m}\boldsymbol{\alpha}_t^{(m)} = q_m^{-1}\mathbf{A}_{1m}^{\perp'}\mathbf{M}_{p_m}(\mathbf{Y}_t^{(m)} - \mathbf{E}_t^{(m)})\1_{q_m}$, we have
\[\boldsymbol{\alpha}_t^{(m)} = q_m^{-1}(\mathbf{A}_{2m}'\mathbf{A}_{1m}^{\perp}\mathbf{A}_{1m}^{\perp '}\mathbf{A}_{2m})^{-1}\mathbf{A}_{2m}'\mathbf{A}_{1m}^{\perp}\mathbf{A}_{1m}^{\perp'}\mathbf{M}_{p_m}(\mathbf{Y}_t^{(m)} - \mathbf{E}_t^{(m)})\1_{q_m}.\]
Similarly,
\[\boldsymbol{\beta}_t^{(m)} = p_m^{-1}(\mathbf{B}_{2m}'\mathbf{B}_{1m}^{\perp}\mathbf{B}_{1m}^{\perp'}\mathbf{B}_{2m})^{-1}\mathbf{B}_{2m}'\mathbf{B}_{1m}^{\perp}\mathbf{B}_{1m}^{\perp'}\mathbf{M}_{q_m}(\mathbf{Y}_t^{(m)} - \mathbf{E}_t^{(m)})'\1_{p_m}.\]
We can then identify $\boldsymbol{\alpha}_t$ and $\boldsymbol{\beta}_t$ as
\begin{align*}
\boldsymbol{\alpha}_t &= (\mathbf{A}_{1m}'\mathbf{A}_{1m})^{-1}\mathbf{A}_{1m}'\{q_m^{-1}\mathbf{M}_{p_m}(\mathbf{Y}_t^{(m)} - \mathbf{E}_t^{(m)})\1_{q_m} - \mathbf{A}_{2m}\boldsymbol{\alpha}_t^{(m)}\},\\
\boldsymbol{\beta}_t &= (\mathbf{B}_{1m}'\mathbf{B}_{1m})^{-1}\mathbf{B}_{1m}'\{p_m^{-1}\mathbf{M}_{q_m}(\mathbf{Y}_t^{(m)} - \mathbf{E}_t^{(m)})'\1_{p_m} - \mathbf{B}_{2m}\boldsymbol{\beta}_t^{(m)}\}.
\end{align*}
(A refinement procedure can be carried out to estimate $\boldsymbol{\alpha}_t$ and $\boldsymbol{\beta}_t$ as an average over all $m\in[M]$, with $\mathbf{A}_{1m}$ and $\mathbf{B}_{1m}$ re-estimated using least squares estimation. This is indeed integrated in our estimation procedure in Section \ref{subsec:estimation}.) 

Define
\begin{equation*}
    \widetilde{\mathbf{Y}}_t^{(m)} := \mathbf{Y}_t^{(m)}-\mathbf{E}_t^{(m)} - c_t\1_{p_m}\1_{q_m}' - \mathbf{a}_t^{(m)}\1_{q_m}' - \1_{p_m}\mathbf{b}_t^{(m)'}.
\end{equation*}
If we know $\mathbf{v}_1^{(m)}$ as a vector aligning more to the direction of the strongest factors in $\mathbf{Q}_m$, and $\mathbf{v}_2^{(m)}$ as such a vector for $\mathbf{J}_m$ (practically this can be done using similar pre-averaging ideas in \cite{ChenLam2024}, which is also integrated in our estimation procedure), then since for $m\neq n$, by (IC2),
\begin{align}
    &\;\;\;\;
    \mathbbm{E}(\widetilde{\mathbf{Y}}_t^{(m)}\mathbf{v}_2^{(m)}\mathbf{v}_2^{(n)'}\widetilde{\mathbf{Y}}_t^{(n)'})
    = \mathbf{Q}_m\mathbbm{E}(\mathbf{G}_t\mathbf{J}_m'\mathbf{v}_2^{(m)}\mathbf{v}_2^{(n)'}\mathbf{J}_n'\mathbf{G}_t')\mathbf{Q}_n' \notag \\
    &=
    \mathbf{Q}_m\mathbbm{E}\Big\{ \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}(\mathbf{G}_t\mathbf{J}_m'\mathbf{v}_2^{(m)}) \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}(\mathbf{G}_t\mathbf{J}_n\mathbf{v}_2^{(n)})' \Big\} \mathbf{Q}_n' \notag \\
    &=
    \mathbf{Q}_m\mathbbm{E}\Big\{ (\mathbf{v}_2^{(m)'} \mathbf{J}_m \otimes \mathbf{I}_{k_r}) \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}(\mathbf{G}_t) \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}'(\mathbf{G}_t) ( \mathbf{J}_m'\mathbf{v}_2^{(m)} \otimes \mathbf{I}_{k_r}) \Big\} \mathbf{Q}_n' \notag \\
    &=
    \mathbf{Q}_m (\mathbf{v}_2^{(m)'} \mathbf{J}_m \otimes\mathbf{I}_{k_r} ) \mathbbm{E}(\textnormal{\textbf{vec}}(\mathbf{G}_t))^{\otimes 2} (\mathbf{J}_n' \mathbf{v}_2^{(n)} \otimes \mathbf{I}_{k_r}) \mathbf{Q}_n' ,
    \label{eqn: tildeY_vv_tildeY}
\end{align}
which is of rank $k_r$ through having $\mathbbm{E}(\textnormal{\textbf{vec}}(\mathbf{G}_t))^{\otimes 2}$ of full rank by (IC3), we can identify $\mathbf{Q}_m$ as the first $k_r$ eigenvectors of
\[\sum_{n=1;n\neq m}^M \{\mathbbm{E}(\widetilde{\mathbf{Y}}_t^{(m)}\mathbf{v}_2^{(m)}\mathbf{v}_2^{(n)'}\widetilde{\mathbf{Y}}_t^{(n)'})\}^{\otimes 2}.\]
Similarly, we can identify $\mathbf{J}_m$ as the first $k_c$ eigenvectors of
\[\sum_{n=1;n\neq m}^M \{\mathbbm{E}(\widetilde{\mathbf{Y}}_t^{(m)'}\mathbf{v}_1^{(m)}\mathbf{v}_1^{(n)'}\widetilde{\mathbf{Y}}_t^{(n)})\}^{\otimes 2}.\]
We can also identify $\mathbf{R}_m$ as the first $k_r^{(m)}$ eigenvectors of
\[\mathbbm{E}(\widetilde{\mathbf{Y}}_t^{(m)}\mathbf{J}_m^{\perp})^{\otimes 2}
= \mathbf{R}_m\mathbbm{E}[\mathbf{F}_t^{(m)}\mathbf{C}_m'\mathbf{J}_m^{\perp}\mathbf{J}_m^{\perp'}\mathbf{C}_m\mathbf{F}_t^{(m)'}]\mathbf{R}_m',\]
which is of full rank since
$\mathbbm{E}(\textnormal{\textbf{vec}}(\mathbf{F}_t^{(m)}))^{\otimes 2}$ and $\mathbf{J}_m^{\perp'}\mathbf{C}_m$ have full rank by (IC3). Similarly, $\mathbf{C}_m$ can be identified as the first $k_c^{(m)}$ eigenvectors of
\[\mathbbm{E}(\widetilde{\mathbf{Y}}_t^{(m)'}\mathbf{Q}_m^{\perp})^{\otimes 2} = \mathbf{C}_m\mathbbm{E}[\mathbf{F}_t^{(m)'}\mathbf{R}_m'\mathbf{Q}_m^{\perp}\mathbf{Q}_m^{\perp'}\mathbf{R}_m\mathbf{F}_t^{(m)}]\mathbf{C}_m'.\]
Then $\mathbf{F}_t^{(m)}$ can be identified as
\[\mathbf{F}_t^{(m)} = (\mathbf{R}_m'\mathbf{Q}_m^{\perp}\mathbf{Q}_m^{\perp'}\mathbf{R}_m)^{-1}\mathbf{R}_m'\mathbf{Q}_m^{\perp}\mathbf{Q}_m^{\perp'}\widetilde{\mathbf{Y}}_t^{(m)}\mathbf{C}_m.\]
Finally $\mathbf{G}_t$ can be identified as
\[\mathbf{G}_t = \mathbf{Q}_m'(\widetilde{\mathbf{Y}}_t^{(m)} - \mathbf{R}_m\mathbf{F}_t^{(m)}\mathbf{C}_m')\mathbf{J}_m.\]
Again, we can consider the average of the above over all $m\in[M]$ as an estimator of $\mathbf{G}_t$, and re-estimate $\mathbf{Q}_m$ and $\mathbf{J}_m$ using least square method, which is indeed integrated into our estimation procedure. $\square$

title: Proof
body_md:
Recall $\widecheck{\mathbf{G}}_{t,m}$ from Lemma~\ref{lemma: aligned_projected_cores} and we can write
\begin{align*}
    &\;\quad
    \widecheck{\mathbf{G}}_{t,m} 
    = \widecheck{\mathbf{Q}}_m' \mathbf{Q}_m \mathbf{G}_t\mathbf{J}_m' \widecheck{\mathbf{J}}_m  \\
    &=  
    (\mathbf{Q}_m'\mathbf{Q}_m)^{-1/2} \mathbf{Q}_m'\mathbf{Q}_m \mathbf{G}_t \mathbf{J}_m'\mathbf{J}_m (\mathbf{J}_m'\mathbf{J}_m)^{-1/2}
    = 
    (\mathbf{Q}_m'\mathbf{Q}_m)^{1/2} \mathbf{G}_t  (\mathbf{J}_m'\mathbf{J}_m)^{1/2} ,
\end{align*}
so that for the reference group $m_0$, we have $\widecheck{\mathbf{G}}_{t,m_0} = \widecheck{\mathbf{G}}_t$, 
where $\widecheck{\mathbf{G}}_t = \big( \mathbf{Q}_{m_0}'\mathbf{Q}_{m_0} \big)^{1/2} \mathbf{G}_t \big( \mathbf{J}_{m_0}'\mathbf{J}_{m_0} \big)^{1/2}$ as defined in the statement of Theorem~\ref{thm:common_comp_global}.


For each group $m\in[M]$ and $t\in[T]$, define the population quantities
\begin{align*}
    & \boldsymbol{\Xi}_{Q,m}^* := 
     \mathbf{H}_{Q,m_0}'
     \big( \mathbf{Q}_{m_0}'\mathbf{Q}_{m_0} \big)^{1/2} \big( \mathbf{Q}_m'\mathbf{Q}_m \big)^{-1/2} \mathbf{H}_{Q,m} , \\
    & \boldsymbol{\Xi}_{J,m}^* := 
    \mathbf{H}_{J,m_0}'
    \big( \mathbf{J}_{m_0}'\mathbf{J}_{m_0} \big)^{1/2} \big( \mathbf{J}_m'\mathbf{J}_m \big)^{-1/2} \mathbf{H}_{J,m} , \\
    & \mathbf{G}_{t,m}^* :=
    \mathbf{H}_{Q,m}' \big( \mathbf{Q}_m'\mathbf{Q}_m \big)^{1/2} \mathbf{G}_t \big( \mathbf{J}_m'\mathbf{J}_m \big)^{1/2} \mathbf{H}_{J,m} .
\end{align*}
First, note that for all $t\in[T]$,
\begin{align}
    \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}\big( \mathbf{G}_{t,m_0}^* \big) =
    \big( \boldsymbol{\Xi}_{J,m}^* \otimes \boldsymbol{\Xi}_{Q,m}^* \big) \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}\big( \mathbf{G}_{t,m}^* \big) 
    +
    o_P\Big(
    p_m^{\delta_{q,1}^{(m)}/2}
    q_m^{\delta_{j,1}^{(m)}/2}
    \Big) . 
    \label{eqn: Gt_m0_pop}
\end{align}
As $\mathbf{H}_{Q,m}$ and $\mathbf{H}_{J,m}$ are asymptotically orthogonal by Lemmas~\ref{lemma: common_comp_global_local_init} and \ref{lemma: aligned_projected_cores_rot_rate}, 
it also holds that
\begin{align*}
    \boldsymbol{\Xi}_{Q,m}^* \mathbf{H}_{Q,m}' \big( \mathbf{Q}_m'\mathbf{Q}_m \big)^{1/2}
    &=
    \mathbf{H}_{Q,m_0}'
    \big( \mathbf{Q}_{m_0}'\mathbf{Q}_{m_0} \big)^{1/2}
    \big( \mathbf{Q}_m'\mathbf{Q}_m \big)^{-1/2}
    \mathbf{H}_{Q,m} \mathbf{H}_{Q,m}'
    \big( \mathbf{Q}_m'\mathbf{Q}_m \big)^{1/2}
    \\
    &=
    \mathbf{H}_{Q,m_0}'
    \big( \mathbf{Q}_{m_0}'\mathbf{Q}_{m_0} \big)^{1/2}
    + O_P\Big( \eta_{Q,m}^{1/2} p_{m_0}^{\delta_{q,1}^{(m_0)}/2} \Big),
    \\
    \boldsymbol{\Xi}_{J,m}^* \mathbf{H}_{J,m}' \big( \mathbf{J}_m'\mathbf{J}_m \big)^{1/2}
    &=
    \mathbf{H}_{J,m_0}'
    \big( \mathbf{J}_{m_0}'\mathbf{J}_{m_0} \big)^{1/2}
    \big( \mathbf{J}_m'\mathbf{J}_m \big)^{-1/2}
    \mathbf{H}_{J,m} \mathbf{H}_{J,m}'
    \big( \mathbf{J}_m'\mathbf{J}_m \big)^{1/2} \\
    &=
    \mathbf{H}_{J,m_0}'
    \big( \mathbf{J}_{m_0}'\mathbf{J}_{m_0} \big)^{1/2}
    +
    O_P\Big( 
    \eta_{J,m}^{1/2}
    q_{m_0}^{\delta_{j,1}^{(m_0)}/2} \Big).
\end{align*}
so that together with $\lambda_{\min}\big( \mathbf{Q}_{m_0}'\mathbf{Q}_{m_0} \big) \lambda_{\min}\big( \mathbf{J}_{m_0}'\mathbf{J}_{m_0} \big) = O\big\{ \lambda_{\min}\big( \mathbf{Q}_m'\mathbf{Q}_m \big) \lambda_{\min}\big( \mathbf{J}_m'\mathbf{J}_m \big) \big\}$ from the statement of Theorem~\ref{thm:common_comp_global},
we arrive at
\begin{align}
    &\;\quad
    \boldsymbol{\Xi}_{Q,m}^* \mathbf{G}_{t,m}^* \boldsymbol{\Xi}_{J,m}^{*\prime}
    =
    \boldsymbol{\Xi}_{Q,m}^* \mathbf{H}_{Q,m}' \big( \mathbf{Q}_m'\mathbf{Q}_m \big)^{1/2} \mathbf{G}_t \big( \mathbf{J}_m'\mathbf{J}_m \big)^{1/2}  \mathbf{H}_{J,m} \boldsymbol{\Xi}_{J,m}^{*\prime} \notag \\
    &=
    \mathbf{H}_{Q,m_0}'
    \big( \mathbf{Q}_{m_0}'\mathbf{Q}_{m_0} \big)^{1/2} 
    \mathbf{G}_t
    \big( \mathbf{J}_{m_0}'\mathbf{J}_{m_0} \big)^{1/2} 
    \mathbf{H}_{J,m_0}
    + O_P\big( 
    \eta_{Q,m}^{1/2}
    \eta_{J,m}^{1/2}
    p_{m}^{\delta_{q,1}^{(m)} /2} q_{m}^{\delta_{j,1}^{(m)} /2} \big) \notag \\
    &=
    \mathbf{G}_{t,m_0}^* 
    + O_P\big( 
    \eta_{Q,m}^{1/2}
    \eta_{J,m}^{1/2}
    p_{m}^{\delta_{q,1}^{(m)} /2} q_{m}^{\delta_{j,1}^{(m)} /2} \big) 
    =
    \mathbf{H}_{Q,m_0}' \widecheck{\mathbf{G}}_t  \mathbf{H}_{J,m_0}
    + O_P\big( 
    \eta_{Q,m}^{1/2}
    \eta_{J,m}^{1/2}
    p_{m}^{\delta_{q,1}^{(m)} /2} q_{m}^{\delta_{j,1}^{(m)} /2} \big) .
    \label{eqn: XiQ_G_XiJ_pop}
\end{align}
Also by Lemma~\ref{lemma: aligned_projected_cores}, we have
\begin{align}
    \widehat{\mathbf{G}}_{t,m} = 
    \mathbf{G}_{t,m}^* + O_P(\Delta_{G,m}^{1/2}) 
    =
    \mathbf{H}_{Q,m}' \big( \mathbf{Q}_m'\mathbf{Q}_m \big)^{1/2} \mathbf{G}_t \big( \mathbf{J}_m'\mathbf{J}_m \big)^{1/2} \mathbf{H}_{J,m} + O_P( \Delta_{G,m}^{1/2} ) ,
    \label{eqn: wh_Gt_m}
\end{align}
where $O_P(\cdot)$ is in terms of Frobenius norm,
and $\Delta_{G,m}$ is defined in the statement of Theorem~\ref{thm:common_comp_global} such that
\[
\Delta_{G,m} = 
\min(p_m,q_m)
    + p_m^{\delta_{r,1}^{(m)}}
    q_m^{\delta_{c,1}^{(m)}}
    \big( \Delta_{R,m} + \Delta_{C,m} + \Delta_{F,m} \big)
    + \big( \eta_{Q,m} + \eta_{J,m} \big) p_m q_m .
\]
By the construction of $\widehat{\mathbf{Z}}_{G,m}$ in Step~3 of Section~\ref{subsec:estimation} and with $\widehat{\mathbf{G}}_{t,m}$ defined in Lemma~\ref{lemma: aligned_projected_cores},
note that
\begin{align*}
    \widehat{\mathbf{Z}}_{G,m} &= 
    \left( \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}(\widehat{\mathbf{Q}}_m'\widecheck{\mathbf{Y}}_{G,1}^{(m)}\widehat{\mathbf{J}}_m), \dots, \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}(\widehat{\mathbf{Q}}_m'\widecheck{\mathbf{Y}}_{G,T}^{(m)}\widehat{\mathbf{J}}_m) \right)
    = 
    \left( \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}(\widehat{\mathbf{G}}_{1,m}), \dots, \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}(\widehat{\mathbf{G}}_{T,m}) \right) .
\end{align*}
Then we may define the population version of $\widehat{\mathbf{Z}}_{G,m}$ as $\mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^* := \left( \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}(\mathbf{G}_{1,m}^*), \dots, \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}(\mathbf{G}_{T,m}^*) \right)$,
so that by \eqref{eqn: wh_Gt_m}, we have
\begin{align}
    \big\| \widehat{\mathbf{Z}}_{G,m} - \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^* \big\|_F^2
    \lesssim_P
    T \cdot \Delta_{G,m} .
    \label{eqn: Z_Gm_est_rate}
\end{align}


Next, recall the matrix $\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_{m} = \widehat{\mathbf{Z}}_{G,m_0} \widehat{\mathbf{Z}}_{G,m}' (\widehat{\mathbf{Z}}_{G,m} \widehat{\mathbf{Z}}_{G,m}')^{-1}$ for the two-sided alignment in Step~3 of Section~\ref{subsec:estimation}.
For any group $m\neq m_0$, the population version of $\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_m$ is $\boldsymbol{\Xi}_m^* := \mathbf{Z}_{G,m_0}^* \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^{*\prime} \big( \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^* \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^{*\prime} \big)^{-1}$.
With \eqref{eqn: Gt_m0_pop}, we can write
\begin{align*}
    \mathbf{Z}_{G,m_0}^* &= \left( \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}(\mathbf{G}_{1,m_0}^*), \dots, \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}(\mathbf{G}_{T,m_0}^*) \right) 
    =
    \big( \boldsymbol{\Xi}_{J,m}^* \otimes \boldsymbol{\Xi}_{Q,m}^* \big) \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^* 
    + o_P\Big(
    \big\|
    \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^*
    \big\|_F
    \Big) ,
\end{align*}
which implies
$\boldsymbol{\Xi}_m^* = \mathbf{Z}_{G,m_0}^* \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^{*\prime} \big( \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^* \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^{*\prime} \big)^{-1} 
= \boldsymbol{\Xi}_{J,m}^* \otimes \boldsymbol{\Xi}_{Q,m}^* +o_P(1)$
given Assumption~(S1).
Meanwhile, also by Assumption~(S1), we have
\begin{align}
    \Big\| \big( \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^* \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^{*\prime} \big)^{-1} \Big\|
    = O_P\left( \frac{1}{T S_m} \right) ,
    \label{eqn: global_Gram_inv}
\end{align}
where 
$S_m$ is defined in the main text.
Hence we may expand
\begin{align}
    \widehat{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_m &=
    \big\{ \mathbf{Z}_{G,m_0}^* +
    (\widehat{\mathbf{Z}}_{G,m_0} - \mathbf{Z}_{G,m_0}^*) \big\}
    \big\{ \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^* +
    (\widehat{\mathbf{Z}}_{G,m} - \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^*)
    \big\}' \notag \\
    &\;\quad
    \cdot
    \Big[ \big\{ \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^* +
    (\widehat{\mathbf{Z}}_{G,m} - \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^*)
    \big\}
    \big\{ \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^* +
    (\widehat{\mathbf{Z}}_{G,m} - \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^*)
    \big\}' \Big]^{-1} \notag \\
    &=:
    \mathbf{Z}_{G,m_0}^* \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^{*\prime} \big( \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^* \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^{*\prime} \big)^{-1}
    +  \mathcal{R}_{\Xi,m} ,
    \label{eqn: global_hat_Xi_expansion}
\end{align}
where $\mathcal{R}_{\Xi,m}$ denotes all remaining terms in the decomposition and would involve at least one $(\widehat{\mathbf{Z}}_{G,m} - \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^*)$ or $(\widehat{\mathbf{Z}}_{G,m_0} - \mathbf{Z}_{G,m_0}^*)$.
As detailed, we bound all terms in $\mathcal{R}_{\Xi,m}$.
To this end, by \eqref{eqn: Z_Gm_est_rate} and \eqref{eqn: global_Gram_inv}, we first have
\begin{align}
    &\;\quad
    \Big\| (\widehat{\mathbf{Z}}_{G,m_0} - \mathbf{Z}_{G,m_0}^*) \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^{*\prime}
    \big( \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^* \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^{*\prime} \big)^{-1} \Big\|_F^2 
    \lesssim_P
    \big\| \widehat{\mathbf{Z}}_{G,m_0} - \mathbf{Z}_{G,m_0}^* \big\|_F^2
    \cdot \big\| \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^{*\prime} \big\|_F^2
    \cdot \Big\| \big( \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^* \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^{*\prime} \big)^{-1} \Big\|^2 \notag \\
    &=
    O_P\big( T \cdot \Delta_{G,m_0} \big)
    \cdot O_P\big( T S_m \big)
    \cdot O_P\left( (T S_m)^{-2} \right)
    =
    O_P\left( \frac{\Delta_{G,m_0}}{S_m}
    \right) ,
    \label{eqn: global_Xi_error_1}
\end{align}
where $\big\| \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^{*\prime} \big\|_F^2 = O_P(T S_m)$ used Assumption~(F1).
Similarly,
\begin{align}
    &\;\quad
    \Big\| \mathbf{Z}_{G,m_0}^*
    (\widehat{\mathbf{Z}}_{G,m} - \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^*)'
    \big( \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^* \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^{*\prime} \big)^{-1}
    \Big\|_F^2 
    \lesssim_P
    \big\| \mathbf{Z}_{G,m_0}^* \big\|^2
    \cdot \big\| \widehat{\mathbf{Z}}_{G,m} - \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^* \big\|_F^2
    \cdot \Big\| \big( \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^* \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^{*\prime} \big)^{-1} \Big\|^2 \notag \\
    &= 
    O_P\big( T S_{m_0} \big)
    \cdot O_P\big( T\cdot \Delta_{G,m} \big)
    \cdot O_P\left( (T S_m)^{-2} \right)
    = 
    O_P\left( \frac{\Delta_{G,m} S_{m_0} }{S_{m}^2}
    \right) .
    \label{eqn: global_Xi_error_2}
\end{align}
To bound the cross term in $\mathcal{R}_{\Xi,m}$ involving both
$\widehat{\mathbf{Z}}_{G,m_0} - \mathbf{Z}_{G,m_0}^*$ and
$\widehat{\mathbf{Z}}_{G,m} - \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^*$,
let $\mathbf{E}_{G,m} := \widehat{\mathbf{Z}}_{G,m} - \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^*$.
By the condition $\Delta_{G,m} = o\big\{ \lambda_{\min}\big( \mathbf{Q}_m'\mathbf{Q}_m \big) \lambda_{\min}\big( \mathbf{J}_m'\mathbf{J}_m \big) \big\}$ in the statement of Theorem~\ref{thm:common_comp_global},
we have $\Delta_{G,m} = o(S_m)$.
Then the cross term satisfies
\begin{align}
    &\;\quad
    \Big\| \mathbf{E}_{G,m_0} \mathbf{E}_{G,m}'
    \Big[ \big( \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^* + \mathbf{E}_{G,m} \big) 
    \big( \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^* + \mathbf{E}_{G,m}
    \big)' \Big]^{-1} \Big\|_F^2 \notag \\
    &\lesssim_P
    \big\| \mathbf{E}_{G,m_0} \big\|_F^2
    \big\| \mathbf{E}_{G,m} \big\|_F^2
    \Big\| \big[ \big( \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^* + \mathbf{E}_{G,m} \big)
    \big( \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^* + \mathbf{E}_{G,m} \big)' \Big]^{-1} \Big\|^2 \notag \\
    &\lesssim_P
    \big( T\Delta_{G,m_0} \big) 
    \big( T\Delta_{G,m} \big)
    \big( T^{-2} S_m^{-2} \big) 
    =
    \frac{\Delta_{G,m_0} \Delta_{G,m}}{ S_m^2 }
    ,
    \label{eqn: global_cross_Xi}
\end{align}
where we used $\Big\| \big[ \big( \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^* + \mathbf{E}_{G,m} \big) \big( \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^* + \mathbf{E}_{G,m} \big)' \Big]^{-1} \Big\|^2 \lesssim_P T^{-2} S_m^{-2}$, which follows from applying Weyl's inequality on $\lambda_{\min}\big( A_m \big) = O_P(T S_m)$ (as in \eqref{eqn: ZZ_diff_inv_gram_pert} below), combined with \eqref{eqn: global_Bm_bound} and $\Delta_{G,m} = o(S_m)$.


Finally, we bound
\begin{align}
    \mathbf{Z}_{G,m_0}^* \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^{*\prime}
    \Big\{ \big( \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^* \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^{*\prime} \big)^{-1}
    - \big( \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^* \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^{*\prime}
    + B_m \big)^{-1} \Big\}
    =
    \mathbf{Z}_{G,m_0}^* \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^{*\prime} \Big\{ A_m^{-1} - \big( A_m + B_m \big)^{-1} \Big\} ,
    \label{eqn: ZZ_diff_inv_gram_pert}
\end{align}
where $A_m := \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^* \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^{*\prime}$
and $B_m := \mathbf{E}_{G,m} \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^{*\prime} + \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^* \mathbf{E}_{G,m}' + \mathbf{E}_{G,m} \mathbf{E}_{G,m}'$.
Note that $\lambda_{\min}\big( A_m \big) = O_P(T S_m)$ by Assumption~(S1) and the definition of $S_m$.
Also, by the condition $\Delta_{G,m} = o(S_m)$ from the statement of Theorem~\ref{thm:common_comp_global} and \eqref{eqn: Z_Gm_est_rate}, we have
\begin{align}
    \big\| B_m \big\|
    &\lesssim_P
    \big\| \mathbf{E}_{G,m} \big\|_F
    \big\| \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^* \big\| +
    \big\| \mathbf{E}_{G,m} \big\|_F^2
    =
    O_P\Big(
    \sqrt{T \Delta_{G,m}}
    \cdot \sqrt{T S_m} \Big)
    + O_P\big( T \Delta_{G,m} \big) 
    =
    O_P\Big( T \sqrt{ \Delta_{G,m} S_m} \Big),
    \label{eqn: global_Bm_bound}
\end{align}
where we used $\big\| \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^* \big\|^2 \asymp_P T S_m$ under Assumptions~(S1) and (F1).

Using the matrix identity $\mathbf{A}^{-1} - (\mathbf{A}+\mathbf{B})^{-1} = \mathbf{A}^{-1} \mathbf{B} (\mathbf{A} + \mathbf{B})^{-1}$ for any matrices $\mathbf{A}, \mathbf{B}$,
we obtain
\begin{align*}
    &\;\quad
    \Big\| A_m^{-1}
    - \big( A_m + B_m \big)^{-1} \Big\| 
    \leq
    \big\| A_m^{-1} \big\|
    \big\| B_m \big\|
    \Big\| \big( A_m + B_m \big)^{-1} \Big\| \notag \\
    &=
    O_P\Big( 
    T^{-1} S_m^{-1} T \sqrt{ \Delta_{G,m} S_m} T^{-1} S_m^{-1}
    \Big) 
    =
    O_P\Big( 
    T^{-1} S_m^{-3/2} \Delta_{G,m}^{1/2}
    \Big) .
\end{align*}
Hence the corresponding term in $\mathcal{R}_{\Xi,m}$ from \eqref{eqn: ZZ_diff_inv_gram_pert} is bounded by
\begin{align}
    &\;\quad
    \Big\| \mathbf{Z}_{G,m_0}^* \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^{*\prime}
    \Big[ A_m^{-1} - \big( A_m + B_m \big)^{-1} \Big] \Big\|_F^2 
    \lesssim
    \big\| \mathbf{Z}_{G,m_0}^* \big\|^2
    \big\| \mathbf{Z}_{G,m}^* \big\|^2
    \Big\| A_m^{-1} - \big( A_m + B_m \big)^{-1} \Big\|^2 \notag \\
    &=
    O_P\Big(
    T S_{m_0}
    T S_m
    T^{-2}
    S_m^{-3}
    \Delta_{G,m}
    \Big)
    =
    O_P\left(
    \frac{ S_{m_0}}{S_m^2}
    \Delta_{G,m}
    \right)
    = 
    O_P\left(
    \frac{\Delta_{G,m}}{S_m}
    \right) ,
    \label{eqn: global_inv_gram_term}
\end{align}
where the last equality used $\lambda_{\min}\big( \mathbf{Q}_{m_0}'\mathbf{Q}_{m_0} \big) \lambda_{\min}\big( \mathbf{J}_{m_0}'\mathbf{J}_{m_0} \big)
= O\big\{ \lambda_{\min}\big( \mathbf{Q}_m'\mathbf{Q}_m \big) \lambda_{\min}\big( \mathbf{J}_m'\mathbf{J}_m \big) \big\}$ so that $S_{m_0} = O(S_m)$ from the statement of Theorem~\ref{thm:common_comp_global}.


Combining \eqref{eqn: global_Xi_error_1}, 
\eqref{eqn: global_Xi_error_2}, 
\eqref{eqn: global_cross_Xi}, 
and \eqref{eqn: global_inv_gram_term},
we conclude $\|\mathcal{R}_{\Xi,m}\|_F^2 = O_P(\Delta_{G,m_0}/S_m + \Delta_{G,m} / S_m)$, and thus
\begin{align}
    \big\| \widehat{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_m - \boldsymbol{\Xi}_m^* \big\|_F^2
    \lesssim_P
    \max_{m'\in[M]} \frac{\Delta_{G,m'}}{S_{m'}} .
    \label{eqn: global_hat_Xi_rate}
\end{align}



Next, recall from Step~3 of Section~\ref{subsec:estimation} the definition of the notation $\mathcal{R}(\mathbf{W})$ for a block matrix $\mathbf{W} = (\mathbf{W}_{ij})_{i\in[k_c], j\in[k_c]}$, with each $\mathbf{W}_{ij}$ of size $k_r\times k_r$, such that
\begin{align*}
    \mathcal{R}(\mathbf{W}) = (\textnormal{\textbf{vec}}(\mathbf{W}_{11}),\ldots,\textnormal{\textbf{vec}}(\mathbf{W}_{k_c1}),\ldots,\textnormal{\textbf{vec}}(\mathbf{W}_{1k_c}),\ldots,\textnormal{\textbf{vec}}(\mathbf{W}_{k_ck_c})).
\end{align*}
Note that $\mathcal{R}(\cdot)$ is a fixed permutation of the entries of the matrix input and hence preserves the Frobenius norm.
Thus, $\big\| \mathcal{R}(\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_m) - \mathcal{R}(\boldsymbol{\Xi}_m^*) \big\|_F = \big\| \widehat{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_m - \boldsymbol{\Xi}_m^* \big\|_F$, and hence by \eqref{eqn: global_hat_Xi_rate},
\begin{align}
    \big\| \mathcal{R}(\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_m) - \mathcal{R}(\boldsymbol{\Xi}_m^*) \big\|_F^2
    =
    O_P\Bigg(
    \max_{m'\in[M]} \frac{\Delta_{G,m'}}{S_{m'}}
    \Bigg) .
    \label{eqn: global_R_Xi_perturbation}
\end{align}

By construction in Step~3 of Section~\ref{subsec:estimation},
the matrix $\widehat{\sigma}_{\Xi,m} \widehat{\mathbf{u}}_{\Xi,m} \widehat{\mathbf{v}}_{\Xi,m}'$ is the rank-1 singular value decomposition of $\mathcal{R}(\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_m)$.
Then let $\sigma_{\Xi,m}^* \mathbf{u}_{\Xi,m}^* \mathbf{v}_{\Xi,m}^{*\prime}$ be the rank-1 singular value decomposition of $\mathcal{R}(\boldsymbol{\Xi}_m^*)$.
From Lemma~\ref{lemma: alignment_equality}, we have
\[
\mathcal{R}\big( \widehat{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_{J,m} \otimes \widehat{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_{Q,m} \big)
= 
\widehat{\sigma}_{\Xi,m} \widehat{\mathbf{u}}_{\Xi,m} \widehat{\mathbf{v}}_{\Xi,m}' .
\]
Recall previously that $\boldsymbol{\Xi}_m^* = \boldsymbol{\Xi}_{J,m}^* \otimes \boldsymbol{\Xi}_{Q,m}^*$, and by analogous arguments in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lemma: alignment_equality}, we also have
\[
\sigma_{\Xi,m}^* \mathbf{u}_{\Xi,m}^* \mathbf{v}_{\Xi,m}^{*\prime} 
= \mathcal{R}\big( \boldsymbol{\Xi}_{J,m}^* \otimes \boldsymbol{\Xi}_{Q,m}^* \big)
= \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}\big( \boldsymbol{\Xi}_{Q,m}^* \big) \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}\big( \boldsymbol{\Xi}_{J,m}^* \big)' ,
\]
which implies
\begin{align}
    \sigma_{\Xi,m}^* = \big\| \boldsymbol{\Xi}_{Q,m}^* \big\|_F \cdot \big\| \boldsymbol{\Xi}_{J,m}^* \big\|_F
    =O_P( 1 ) ,
    \label{eqn: sigma_Xi_m_pop}
\end{align}
where we used the definitions of $\boldsymbol{\Xi}_{Q,m}^*$ and $\boldsymbol{\Xi}_{J,m}^*$ at the beginning of this proof, together with the rate condition $\lambda_{\min}\big( \mathbf{Q}_{m_0}'\mathbf{Q}_{m_0} \big) \lambda_{\min}\big( \mathbf{J}_{m_0}'\mathbf{J}_{m_0} \big) = O\big\{ \lambda_{\min}\big( \mathbf{Q}_m'\mathbf{Q}_m \big) \lambda_{\min}\big( \mathbf{J}_m'\mathbf{J}_m \big) \big\}$ in the statement of Theorem~\ref{thm:common_comp_global}.
Altogether, using the fact that $\mathcal{R}(\cdot)$ preserves the Frobenius norm (as in \eqref{eqn: global_R_Xi_perturbation}), we have
\begin{align}
    &\;\quad
    \Big\| \widehat{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_{J,m} \otimes \widehat{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_{Q,m}
    - \boldsymbol{\Xi}_{J,m}^* \otimes \boldsymbol{\Xi}_{Q,m}^* \Big\|_F^2
    =
    \Big\| \mathcal{R}(\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_{J,m} \otimes \widehat{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_{Q,m})
    - \mathcal{R}(\boldsymbol{\Xi}_{J,m}^* \otimes \boldsymbol{\Xi}_{Q,m}^*) \Big\|_F^2 \notag \\
    &=
    \Big\| \widehat{\sigma}_{\Xi,m} \widehat{\mathbf{u}}_{\Xi,m} \widehat{\mathbf{v}}_{\Xi,m}'
    - \sigma_{\Xi,m}^* \mathbf{u}_{\Xi,m}^* \mathbf{v}_{\Xi,m}^{*\prime} \Big\|_F^2  \notag \\
    &\lesssim
    \big| \widehat{\sigma}_{\Xi,m} - \sigma_{\Xi,m}^* \big|^2
    \cdot \big\| \widehat{\mathbf{u}}_{\Xi,m} \widehat{\mathbf{v}}_{\Xi,m}' \big\|_F^2
    + (\sigma_{\Xi,m}^*)^2 \big\| \widehat{\mathbf{u}}_{\Xi,m} \widehat{\mathbf{v}}_{\Xi,m}'
    - \mathbf{u}_{\Xi,m}^* \mathbf{v}_{\Xi,m}^{*\prime} \big\|_F^2 \notag \\
    &\lesssim_P
    \big\| \mathcal{R}(\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_m) - \mathcal{R}(\boldsymbol{\Xi}_m^*) \big\|_F^2 
    =
    \big\| \widehat{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_m - \boldsymbol{\Xi}_m^* \big\|_F^2 
    =
    O_P\Bigg(
    \max_{m'\in[M]} \frac{\Delta_{G,m'}}{S_{m'}}
    \Bigg) ,
    \label{eqn: global_product_alignment}
\end{align}
where the last line used Weyl's inequality and the Davis--Kahan theorem \citep[Theorem~2]{yu2015useful},
in addition to \eqref{eqn: global_R_Xi_perturbation} and \eqref{eqn: sigma_Xi_m_pop}.


By the construction of the global factor estimator $\widehat{\mathbf{G}}_t$ in Step~3 of Section~\ref{subsec:estimation}, we have
\begin{align}
    &\;\quad
    \Big\| \widehat{\mathbf{G}}_t
    - \mathbf{H}_{Q,m_0}' \widecheck{\mathbf{G}}_t \mathbf{H}_{J,m_0} \Big\|_F^2
    \lesssim
    \max_{m\in[M]}
    \Big\| \widehat{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_{Q,m} \widehat{\mathbf{G}}_{t,m} \widehat{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_{J,m}'
    - \mathbf{H}_{Q,m_0}' \widecheck{\mathbf{G}}_t \mathbf{H}_{J,m_0}
    \Big\|_F^2.
    \label{eqn: global_final_start}
\end{align}
For each fixed $m$, we decompose
\begin{align}
    \widehat{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_{Q,m} \widehat{\mathbf{G}}_{t,m} \widehat{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_{J,m}'
    - \mathbf{H}_{Q,m_0}' \widecheck{\mathbf{G}}_t \mathbf{H}_{J,m_0} 
    &=
    \widehat{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_{Q,m} \big( \widehat{\mathbf{G}}_{t,m} - \mathbf{G}_{t,m}^* \big) \widehat{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_{J,m}' 
    + (\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_{Q,m} \mathbf{G}_{t,m}^* \widehat{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_{J,m}'
    - \mathbf{H}_{Q,m_0}' \widecheck{\mathbf{G}}_t \mathbf{H}_{J,m_0}) \notag \\
    &=:
    \mathcal{I}_{\Xi,G,1} + \mathcal{I}_{\Xi,G,2} .
    \label{eqn: global_final_decomp}
\end{align}
For $\mathcal{I}_{\Xi,G,1}$, by \eqref{eqn: sigma_Xi_m_pop} and \eqref{eqn: wh_Gt_m}, we have
$\big\| \widehat{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_{Q,m} \big\|, \big\| \widehat{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_{J,m} \big\| = O_P(1)$, and
$\big\| \widehat{\mathbf{G}}_{t,m} - \mathbf{G}_{t,m}^* \big\|_F^2 = O_P\big( \Delta_{G,m} \big)$, so that
\begin{align}
    \big\| \mathcal{I}_{\Xi,G,1} \big\|_F^2
    \lesssim_P 
    \Delta_{G,m} .
    \label{eqn: global_final_I1}
\end{align}

For $\mathcal{I}_{\Xi,G,2}$, we can write
\begin{align}
    &\;\quad
    \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}(\mathcal{I}_{\Xi,G,2}) =
    \big( \widehat{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_{J,m} \otimes \widehat{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_{Q,m} \big)
    \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}\big( \mathbf{G}_{t,m}^* \big)
    - \big( \mathbf{H}_{J,m_0}' \otimes \mathbf{H}_{Q,m_0}' \big)
    \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}\big( \widecheck{\mathbf{G}}_t \big) \notag \\
    &=
    \Big[ \big( \widehat{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_{J,m} \otimes \widehat{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_{Q,m} \big)
    - \big( \boldsymbol{\Xi}_{J,m}^* \otimes \boldsymbol{\Xi}_{Q,m}^* \big) \Big]
    \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}\big( \mathbf{G}_{t,m}^* \big) \notag \\
    &\;\quad
    + \Big[ \big(
    \boldsymbol{\Xi}_{J,m}^* \otimes \boldsymbol{\Xi}_{Q,m}^*
    \big)
    \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}\big( \mathbf{G}_{t,m}^* \big)
    - \big( \mathbf{H}_{J,m_0}' \otimes \mathbf{H}_{Q,m_0}' \big)
    \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}\big( \widecheck{\mathbf{G}}_t \big) \Big]
    =:
    \mathcal{I}_{\Xi,G,21}
    + \mathcal{I}_{\Xi,G,22} .
    \label{eqn: global_final_I2_decomp}
\end{align}
In particular, for $\mathcal{I}_{\Xi,G,21}$,
by \eqref{eqn: global_product_alignment} and $\big\| \mathbf{G}_{t,m}^* \big\|_F^2 = O_P(S_m)$,
we have
\begin{align}
    \big\| \mathcal{I}_{\Xi,G,21} \big\|_F^2
    &\lesssim_P
    \Big\| \widehat{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_{J,m} \otimes \widehat{\boldsymbol{\Xi}}_{Q,m} - \boldsymbol{\Xi}_{J,m}^* \otimes \boldsymbol{\Xi}_{Q,m}^* \Big\|_F^2
    \cdot \big\| \mathbf{G}_{t,m}^* \big\|_F^2 
    \lesssim_P
    \max_{m'\in[M]}
    \frac{\Delta_{G,m'}}{S_{m'}}
    S_m .
    \label{eqn: global_final_I21}
\end{align}
Also, by \eqref{eqn: XiQ_G_XiJ_pop},
\begin{align}
    \big\| \mathcal{I}_{\Xi,G,22} \big\|_F^2 &=
    O_P\Big(
    \eta_{Q,m}
    \eta_{J,m}
    p_m^{\delta_{q,1}^{(m)}}
    q_m^{\delta_{j,1}^{(m)}}
    \Big) .
    \label{eqn: global_final_I22}
\end{align}

Combining \eqref{eqn: global_final_start},
\eqref{eqn: global_final_decomp},
\eqref{eqn: global_final_I2_decomp},
\eqref{eqn: global_final_I1}, 
\eqref{eqn: global_final_I21}, 
and \eqref{eqn: global_final_I22}, 
we obtain
\[
\Big\| \widehat{\mathbf{G}}_t - \mathbf{H}_{Q,m_0}' \widecheck{\mathbf{G}}_t \mathbf{H}_{J,m_0} \Big\|_F^2
\lesssim_P
\max_{m\in[M]} \Delta_{G,m}
+ \max_{m'\in[M]} \frac{\Delta_{G,m'}}{S_{m'}} \max_{m\in[M]} S_m 
+ \max_{m\in[M]} \eta_{Q,m} \eta_{J,m} p_m^{\delta_{q,1}^{(m)}} q_m^{\delta_{j,1}^{(m)}}   ,
\]
which thus concludes the proof for $\big\| \widehat{\mathbf{G}}_t - \mathbf{H}_{Q,m_0}' \widecheck{\mathbf{G}}_t \mathbf{H}_{J,m_0} \big\|_F^2$, by noting that the last term above is dominated by the first term.



It remains to derive the rate for the re-estimated global loading matrices $\widetilde{\mathbf{Q}}_m$ and $\widetilde{\mathbf{J}}_m$ in Step~3 of Section~\ref{subsec:estimation}. 
First, as $\mathbf{H}_{Q,m_0}$ and $\mathbf{H}_{J,m_0}$ are asymptotically orthogonal by Lemma~\ref{lemma: aligned_projected_cores_rot_rate}, the population version of the re-estimated Kronecker product matrix is
\begin{align}
    \mathbf{K}_m^0 :=
    \Big\{ \mathbf{J}_m \big( \mathbf{J}_{m_0}'\mathbf{J}_{m_0} \big)^{-1/2} \mathbf{H}_{J,m_0} \Big\}
    \otimes \Big\{ \mathbf{Q}_m \big( \mathbf{Q}_{m_0}'\mathbf{Q}_{m_0} \big)^{-1/2} \mathbf{H}_{Q,m_0} \Big\} .
    \label{eqn: reloading_kron_target}
\end{align}
For each $m\in[M]$, define the matrices
\begin{align*}
    \mathbf{Y}_m &:=
    \Big( \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}\big( \widecheck{\mathbf{Y}}_{G,1}^{(m)} \big),
    \dots,
    \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}\big( \widecheck{\mathbf{Y}}_{G,T}^{(m)} \big) \Big), 
    \quad
    \mathbf{G}^* :=
    \Big( \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}\big( \mathbf{H}_{Q,m_0}' \widecheck{\mathbf{G}}_1 \mathbf{H}_{J,m_0} \big),
    \dots,
    \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}\big( \mathbf{H}_{Q,m_0}' \widecheck{\mathbf{G}}_T \mathbf{H}_{J,m_0} \big) \Big) , \\
    \widehat{\mathbf{G}} &:=
    \Big( \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}\big( \widehat{\mathbf{G}}_1 \big),
    \dots,
    \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}\big( \widehat{\mathbf{G}}_T \big) \Big) ,
    \quad
    \mathbf{U}_m := \mathbf{Y}_m - \mathbf{K}_m^0 \mathbf{G}^* ,
\end{align*}
so that $\mathbf{U}_m$ satisfies
\begin{align}
    \mathbf{U}_m &= \mathbf{Y}_m - \mathbf{K}_m^0 \mathbf{G}^*
    =
    \big( \mathbf{Y}_m - \mathbf{Y}_m^{0}\big)
    + \big( \mathbf{Y}_m^{0} - \mathbf{K}_m^0 \mathbf{G}^* \big) ,
    \label{eqn: reloading_U_decomp}
\end{align}
where $\mathbf{Y}_m^{0}$ denotes the matrix whose columns are $\textnormal{\textbf{vec}}(\mathbf{Q}_m \mathbf{G}_t \mathbf{J}_m')$, $t\in[T]$.
Consider the first term in \eqref{eqn: reloading_U_decomp}, which has columns $\textnormal{\textbf{vec}}\big( \widecheck{\mathbf{Y}}_{G,t}^{(m)} - \mathbf{Q}_m \mathbf{G}_t \mathbf{J}_m' \big)$.
By our already constructed result in Theorem~\ref{thm:common_comp_global} and with the notation $\Delta_G$ in the theorem's statement,
we have $\big\|\widehat{\mathbf{G}} - \mathbf{G}^* \big\|_F^2 = O_P(T \Delta_G)$.
For each $m\in[M]$, by Theorem~\ref{thm:common_comp_global_local_init} and Lemma~\ref{lemma:bound_Delta},
we have
\begin{align}
    \frac{1}{T} \big\| \mathbf{Y}_m - \mathbf{Y}_m^{0} \big\|_F^2
    &=
    \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=1}^{T}
    \big\| \big( \mathbf{R}_m \mathbf{F}_t^{(m)} \mathbf{C}_m'
    - \widehat{\mathbf{R}}_m \widehat{\mathbf{F}}_t^{(m)} \widehat{\mathbf{C}}_m' \big)
    + \mathbf{M}_{p_m} \mathbf{E}_t^{(m)} \mathbf{M}_{q_m} \big\|_F^2 \notag \\
    &\lesssim_P
    p_m^{\delta_{r,1}^{(m)}}
    q_m^{\delta_{c,1}^{(m)}}
    \big( \Delta_{R,m} + \Delta_{C,m} + \Delta_{F,m} \big)
    + p_m q_m .
    \label{eqn: reloading_Utm_rate1}
\end{align}
For the second term in \eqref{eqn: reloading_U_decomp}, for each $t\in[T]$,
\begin{align}
    &\;\quad
    \Big\| \big( \mathbf{Q}_m \big( \mathbf{Q}_{m_0}' \mathbf{Q}_{m_0} \big)^{-1/2} \mathbf{H}_{Q,m_0} \big) 
    \mathbf{H}_{Q,m_0}' \widecheck{\mathbf{G}}_t \mathbf{H}_{J,m_0}
    \big( \mathbf{J}_m \big( \mathbf{J}_{m_0}' \mathbf{J}_{m_0} \big)^{-1/2} \mathbf{H}_{J,m_0} \big)'
    - \mathbf{Q}_m \mathbf{G}_t \mathbf{J}_m' \Big\|_F^2 \notag \\
    &\lesssim_P
    \big( \eta_{Q,m_0} + \eta_{J,m_0} \big)
    \big\| \mathbf{Q}_m \big\|^2
    \big\| \mathbf{J}_m \big\|^2
    \big\| \big( \mathbf{Q}_{m_0}' \mathbf{Q}_{m_0} \big)^{-1/2} \big\|^2
    \big\|  \big( \mathbf{J}_{m_0}' \mathbf{J}_{m_0} \big)^{-1/2} \big\|^2
    \big\| \widecheck{\mathbf{G}}_t \big\|_F^2 \notag \\
    &=
    O_P\Bigg( \big( \eta_{Q,m_0} + \eta_{J,m_0}
    \big)
    \frac{p_m^{\delta_{q,1}^{(m)}}
    q_m^{\delta_{j,1}^{(m)}}}{p_{m_0}^{\delta_{q,k_r}^{(m_0)}}
    q_{m_0}^{\delta_{j,k_c}^{(m_0)}}}
    S_{m_0}
    \Bigg),
    \label{eqn: reloading_Utm_rate2}
\end{align}
where the last line used Assumption~(S1), the definition of $S_{m_0}$ in Theorem~\ref{thm:common_comp_global}, and $\|\widecheck{\mathbf{G}}_t\|_F^2 = O_P(S_{m_0})$.
Combining \eqref{eqn: reloading_U_decomp}, \eqref{eqn: reloading_Utm_rate1}, and \eqref{eqn: reloading_Utm_rate2},
we have
\begin{align}
    \frac{1}{T} \big\| \mathbf{U}_m \big\|_F^2
    \lesssim_P
    p_m^{\delta_{r,1}^{(m)}}
    q_m^{\delta_{c,1}^{(m)}}
    \big( \Delta_{R,m} + \Delta_{C,m} + \Delta_{F,m} \big)
    + p_m q_m
    + \big( \eta_{Q,m_0} + \eta_{J,m_0}
    \big)
    \frac{p_m^{\delta_{q,1}^{(m)}}
    q_m^{\delta_{j,1}^{(m)}}}{p_{m_0}^{\delta_{q,k_r}^{(m_0)}}
    q_{m_0}^{\delta_{j,k_c}^{(m_0)}}}
    S_{m_0} .
    \label{eqn: reloading_Um_rate}
\end{align}

We next bound $\big\| T^{-1}\mathbf{U}_m \widehat{\mathbf{G}}' \big\|_F^2$.
By definition, the $(i,j)$ entry of $T^{-1}\mathbf{U}_m \widehat{\mathbf{G}}'$ is
\begin{align}
    \big( T^{-1}\mathbf{U}_m \widehat{\mathbf{G}}' \big)_{ij}
    = \frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T} \big(\mathbf{U}_m\big)_{it} \big(\widehat{\mathbf{G}}\big)_{jt},
    \label{eqn: reloading_UTG_entry}
\end{align}
where $\big(\mathbf{U}_m\big)_{it}$ denotes the $(i,t)$ entry of $\mathbf{U}_m$ and $\big(\widehat{\mathbf{G}}\big)_{jt}$ denotes the $(j,t)$ entry of $\widehat{\mathbf{G}}$.
Recall the decomposition $\mathbf{U}_m = (\mathbf{Y}_m - \mathbf{Y}_m^0) + (\mathbf{Y}_m^0 - \mathbf{K}_m^0\mathbf{G}^*)$, where $\mathbf{Y}_m^0$ is the matrix whose columns are $\textnormal{\textbf{vec}}(\mathbf{Q}_m\mathbf{G}_t\mathbf{J}_m')$, $t\in[T]$.
Thus we have
\begin{align*}
    \big(\mathbf{U}_m\big)_{it} &=
    \Big[ \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}\big( \widecheck{\mathbf{Y}}_{G,t}^{(m)} - \mathbf{Q}_m \mathbf{G}_t \mathbf{J}_m' \big) \Big]_i
    + \Big[ \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}(\mathbf{Q}_m\mathbf{G}_t\mathbf{J}_m') - \mathbf{K}_m^0 \mathbf{G}^*_{\cdot t} \Big]_i,
\end{align*}
where $\mathbf{G}^*_{\cdot t}$ denotes the $t$-th column of $\mathbf{G}^*$.
By the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality,
\begin{align}
    \big( T^{-1}\mathbf{U}_m \widehat{\mathbf{G}}' \big)_{ij}^2
    &\leq 
    2 \Bigg[ \frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T} \Big[ \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}\big( \widecheck{\mathbf{Y}}_{G,t}^{(m)} - \mathbf{Q}_m \mathbf{G}_t \mathbf{J}_m' \big) \Big]_i \big(\widehat{\mathbf{G}}\big)_{jt} \Bigg]^2
    \notag \\
    &\;\quad 
    + 2 \Bigg[ \frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T} \Big[ \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}(\mathbf{Q}_m\mathbf{G}_t\mathbf{J}_m') - \mathbf{K}_m^0 \mathbf{G}^*_{\cdot t} \Big]_i \big(\widehat{\mathbf{G}}\big)_{jt} \Bigg]^2.
    \label{eqn: reloading_UTG_decomp}
\end{align}
For the second term on the right-hand side of \eqref{eqn: reloading_UTG_decomp},
by \eqref{eqn: reloading_Utm_rate2} and $\|\widehat{\mathbf{G}}\|_F^2 = O_P(T S_{m_0})$, we have
\begin{align}
    &\;\quad
    \Bigg( \frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}
    \Big[ \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}(\mathbf{Q}_m\mathbf{G}_t\mathbf{J}_m') - \mathbf{K}_m^0 \mathbf{G}^*_{\cdot t} \Big]_i \big(\widehat{\mathbf{G}}\big)_{jt}
    \Bigg)^2 \notag \\
    &\lesssim_P
    \frac{1}{T} \frac{1}{p_m q_m}
    \big( \eta_{Q,m_0} + \eta_{J,m_0} \big)
    \frac{p_m^{\delta_{q,1}^{(m)}} q_m^{\delta_{j,1}^{(m)}}}{S_{m_0}}
    S_{m_0}
    =
    \frac{1}{T p_m q_m}
    \big( \eta_{Q,m_0} + \eta_{J,m_0} \big)
    p_m^{\delta_{q,1}^{(m)}} q_m^{\delta_{j,1}^{(m)}} .
    \label{eqn: reloading_UTG_rot}
\end{align}


For the first term on the right-hand side of \eqref{eqn: reloading_UTG_decomp}, we further decompose
\begin{align*}
    \Big[ \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}\big( \widecheck{\mathbf{Y}}_{G,t}^{(m)} - \mathbf{Q}_m \mathbf{G}_t \mathbf{J}_m' \big) \Big]_i
    =
    \Big[ \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}\big( \mathbf{M}_{p_m}\mathbf{E}_t^{(m)}\mathbf{M}_{q_m} \big) \Big]_i
    + \Big[ \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}\big( \mathbf{R}_m\mathbf{F}_t^{(m)}\mathbf{C}_m' - \widehat{\mathbf{R}}_m\widehat{\mathbf{F}}_t^{(m)}\widehat{\mathbf{C}}_m' \big) \Big]_i .
\end{align*}
By Assumption~(E2), the noise process $\{\mathbf{M}_{p_m} \mathbf{E}_t^{(m)} \mathbf{M}_{q_m}\}$ is independent of the factor process $\{\mathbf{G}_t\}$.
By Lemma~\ref{lemma:correlation_Etm}, the entries of $\{\mathbf{M}_{p_m} \mathbf{E}_t^{(m)} \mathbf{M}_{q_m}\}$ have summable autocovariance bounded by $C\rho(\cdot)$.
By Assumptions~(S1), (F1), and (L1), the entries of $\widehat{\mathbf{G}}$ have second moment of order $S_{m_0}$.
Altogether, we obtain
\begin{align}
    \Bigg(
    \frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}
    \Big[ \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}\big( \mathbf{M}_{p_m}\mathbf{E}_t^{(m)}\mathbf{M}_{q_m} \big) \Big]_i
    \big(\widehat{\mathbf{G}}\big)_{jt} \Bigg)^2
    &\lesssim_P
    \frac{S_{m_0}}{T} .
    \label{eqn: reloading_UTG_noise_entry}
\end{align}
For $\mathbf{R}_m\mathbf{F}_t^{(m)}\mathbf{C}_m' - \widehat{\mathbf{R}}_m\widehat{\mathbf{F}}_t^{(m)}\widehat{\mathbf{C}}_m'$, by Assumption~(IC2), the local factor $\mathbf{F}_t^{(m)}$ is uncorrelated with the global factor $\mathbf{G}_t$. Hence by Theorem~\ref{thm:common_comp_global_local_init}, we have
$\big\| \mathbf{R}_m\mathbf{F}_t^{(m)}\mathbf{C}_m' - \widehat{\mathbf{R}}_m\widehat{\mathbf{F}}_t^{(m)}\widehat{\mathbf{C}}_m' \big\|_F^2 \lesssim_P p_m^{\delta_{r,1}^{(m)}} q_m^{\delta_{c,1}^{(m)}} \big( \Delta_{R,m} + \Delta_{C,m} + \Delta_{F,m} \big)$,
so that
\begin{align}
    \Bigg(\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}
    \Big[ \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}\big( \mathbf{R}_m\mathbf{F}_t^{(m)}\mathbf{C}_m' - \widehat{\mathbf{R}}_m\widehat{\mathbf{F}}_t^{(m)}\widehat{\mathbf{C}}_m' \big) \Big]_i
    \big(\widehat{\mathbf{G}}\big)_{jt} \Bigg)^2
    &\lesssim_P
    \frac{1}{T p_m q_m}
    p_m^{\delta_{r,1}^{(m)}} q_m^{\delta_{c,1}^{(m)}}
    \big( \Delta_{R,m} + \Delta_{C,m} + \Delta_{F,m} \big)
    S_{m_0} .
    \label{eqn: reloading_UTG_local_entry}
\end{align}
Combining \eqref{eqn: reloading_UTG_decomp}, 
\eqref{eqn: reloading_UTG_rot},
\eqref{eqn: reloading_UTG_noise_entry}, and \eqref{eqn: reloading_UTG_local_entry},
summing over $i\in[p_m q_m]$ and $j\in[k_r k_c]$, we conclude
\begin{align}
    \Bigg\| \frac{1}{T} \mathbf{U}_m \widehat{\mathbf{G}}' \Bigg\|_F^2
    &\lesssim_P
    \frac{p_m q_m
    + p_m^{\delta_{r,1}^{(m)}} q_m^{\delta_{c,1}^{(m)}}
    \big( \Delta_{R,m} + \Delta_{C,m} + \Delta_{F,m} \big)}{T}
    S_{m_0} \notag \\
    &\;\quad
    + \frac{1}{T} \big( \eta_{Q,m_0} + \eta_{J,m_0} \big)
    p_m^{\delta_{q,1}^{(m)}} q_m^{\delta_{j,1}^{(m)}} 
    \lesssim
    \frac{p_m q_m
    + p_m^{\delta_{r,1}^{(m)}} q_m^{\delta_{c,1}^{(m)}}
    \big( \Delta_{R,m} + \Delta_{C,m} + \Delta_{F,m} \big)}{T}
    S_{m_0} .
    \label{eqn: reloading_UTG_final}
\end{align}




With our notations above, by the construction in Step~3 of Section~\ref{subsec:estimation}, we can write
\begin{align}
    \widehat{\mathbf{J}_m\otimes\mathbf{Q}_m} &=
    \mathbf{Y}_m \widehat{\mathbf{G}}' \big( \widehat{\mathbf{G}} \widehat{\mathbf{G}}' \big)^{-1}
    =
    \big( \mathbf{K}_m^0 \mathbf{G}^* + \mathbf{U}_m \big)
    \widehat{\mathbf{G}}' \big( \widehat{\mathbf{G}} \widehat{\mathbf{G}}' \big)^{-1} \notag \\
    &=
    \mathbf{K}_m^0 
    + \mathbf{K}_m^0 \big( \mathbf{G}^* \widehat{\mathbf{G}}' - \widehat{\mathbf{G}} \widehat{\mathbf{G}}' \big) \big( \widehat{\mathbf{G}} \widehat{\mathbf{G}}' \big)^{-1} 
    + \mathbf{U}_m \widehat{\mathbf{G}}' \big( \widehat{\mathbf{G}} \widehat{\mathbf{G}}' \big)^{-1} .
    \label{eqn: reloading_decomp}
\end{align}


We bound the two terms in \eqref{eqn: reloading_decomp}. 
First, by Assumption~(S1), the smallest eigenvalue of $T^{-1} \mathbf{G}^* \mathbf{G}^{*\prime}$ is of order $S_{m_0}$. Then we obtain
\begin{align}
    \Big\| \big( \widehat{\mathbf{G}} \widehat{\mathbf{G}}' \big)^{-1} \Big\|
    = O_P\Big( T^{-1} S_{m_0}^{-1} \Big).
    \label{eqn: reloading_inv}
\end{align}
Also, note that $\big\| \mathbf{G}^* \big\|_F^2 = O_P\big( T S_{m_0} \big)$ and $\big\| \widehat{\mathbf{G}} \big\|_F^2  = O_P\big( T S_{m_0} \big)$.
Then for the first term in \eqref{eqn: reloading_decomp}, we have
\begin{align}
    &\;\quad
    \Bigg\| \mathbf{K}_m^0 \big( \mathbf{G}^* \widehat{\mathbf{G}}'
    - \widehat{\mathbf{G}} \widehat{\mathbf{G}}' \big)
    \big( \widehat{\mathbf{G}} \widehat{\mathbf{G}}' \big)^{-1} \Bigg\|_F^2 
    \lesssim
    \big\| \mathbf{K}_m^0 \big\|^2
    \big\| \mathbf{G}^* - \widehat{\mathbf{G}} \big\|_F^2
    \big\| \widehat{\mathbf{G}} \big\|^2
    \Big\| \big( \widehat{\mathbf{G}} \widehat{\mathbf{G}}' \big)^{-1} \Big\|^2 \notag \\
    &=
    O_P\Bigg(
    \big\| \mathbf{K}_m^0 \big\|^2
    \cdot T \Delta_G
    \cdot T S_{m_0}
    \cdot T^{-2} S_{m_0}^{-2}
    \Bigg)
    =
    O_P\Bigg(
    \big\| \mathbf{K}_m^0 \big\|^2
    \frac{ \Delta_G}{S_{m_0} }
    \Bigg) .
    \label{eqn: reloading_term1}
\end{align}
For the second term in \eqref{eqn: reloading_decomp}, 
by \eqref{eqn: reloading_UTG_final} and \eqref{eqn: reloading_inv}
we have
\begin{align}
    &\;\quad
    \Bigg\| \mathbf{U}_m \widehat{\mathbf{G}}' \big( \widehat{\mathbf{G}} \widehat{\mathbf{G}}' \big)^{-1} \Bigg\|_F^2 
    =
    \Bigg\| \Big(\frac{1}{T} \mathbf{U}_m \widehat{\mathbf{G}}' \Big) \Big( \frac{1}{T} \widehat{\mathbf{G}} \widehat{\mathbf{G}}' \Big)^{-1} \Bigg\|_F^2 
    \lesssim_P
    \Big\| \frac{1}{T} \mathbf{U}_m \widehat{\mathbf{G}}' \Big\|_F^2
    \cdot \Big\| \Big( \frac{1}{T} \widehat{\mathbf{G}} \widehat{\mathbf{G}}' \Big)^{-1} \Big\|^2 \notag \\
    &=
    O_P\Bigg(
    \frac{S_{m_0}}{T}
    \big\{ p_m q_m
    + p_m^{\delta_{r,1}^{(m)}} q_m^{\delta_{c,1}^{(m)}}
    \big( \Delta_{R,m} + \Delta_{C,m} + \Delta_{F,m} \big)\big\}
    \cdot S_{m_0}^{-2}
    \Bigg) \notag \\
    &=
    O_P\Bigg(
    \frac{ p_m q_m
    + p_m^{\delta_{r,1}^{(m)}} q_m^{\delta_{c,1}^{(m)}}
    \big( \Delta_{R,m} + \Delta_{C,m} + \Delta_{F,m} \big)}{T S_{m_0}}
    \Bigg) .
    \label{eqn: reloading_term2}
\end{align}


Combining \eqref{eqn: reloading_decomp}, 
\eqref{eqn: reloading_term1}, 
and \eqref{eqn: reloading_term2}, 
we arrive at
\begin{align}
    \Bigg\| \widehat{\mathbf{J}_m\otimes\mathbf{Q}_m}
    - \mathbf{K}_m^0 \Bigg\|_F^2 
    &\lesssim_P
    \big\| \mathbf{K}_m^0 \big\|^2
    \frac{ \Delta_G }{ S_{m_0} }
    +
    \frac{ p_m q_m
    + p_m^{\delta_{r,1}^{(m)}} q_m^{\delta_{c,1}^{(m)}}
    \big( \Delta_{R,m} + \Delta_{C,m} + \Delta_{F,m} \big)}{T S_{m_0}}  
    = \Delta_{K,m}  ,
    \label{eqn: reloading_final_rate}
\end{align}
where the last equality used the definition of $\Delta_{K,m}$ in the statement of Theorem~\ref{thm:common_comp_global}, the fact that $\|\mathbf{K}_m^0\|_F^2 = O_P\big( p_m^{\delta_{q,1}^{(m)}}  q_m^{\delta_{j,1}^{(m)}} /S_{m_0} \big)$ which is direct from \eqref{eqn: reloading_kron_target},
and the condition from the statement of Theorem~\ref{thm:common_comp_global} that
$\lambda_{\min}\big( \mathbf{Q}_{m_0}'\mathbf{Q}_{m_0} \big) \lambda_{\min}\big( \mathbf{J}_{m_0}'\mathbf{J}_{m_0} \big)
= O\big\{ \lambda_{\min}\big( \mathbf{Q}_m'\mathbf{Q}_m \big) \lambda_{\min}\big( \mathbf{J}_m'\mathbf{J}_m \big) \big\}$
and thus 
\[
\frac{p_m^{\delta_{r,1}^{(m)}} q_m^{\delta_{c,1}^{(m)}}
\big( \Delta_{R,m} + \Delta_{C,m} + \Delta_{F,m} \big)}{T S_{m_0}}
\lesssim
\frac{\Delta_{G,m}}{T S_{m_0}}
\lesssim
\frac{\Delta_{G,m}}{S_{m_0}} \frac{1}{T} \frac{p_m^{\delta_{q,1}^{(m)}}  q_m^{\delta_{j,1}^{(m)}}}{S_{m_0}}
= o\left( \big\| \mathbf{K}_m^0 \big\|^2 \frac{ \Delta_G }{ S_{m_0} } \right) .
\]


The remaining arguments are similar to the previous ones in this proof on $\big\| \widehat{\mathbf{G}}_t - \mathbf{H}_{Q,m_0}' \widecheck{\mathbf{G}}_t \mathbf{H}_{J,m_0} \big\|_F^2$.
In particular, by the construction in Step~3 of Section~\ref{subsec:estimation}, the matrix $\mathcal{R}(\widehat{\mathbf{J}_m \otimes \mathbf{Q}_m})$ has a rank-1 singular value decomposition
\begin{align}
    \mathcal{R}\big( \widehat{\mathbf{J}_m\otimes\mathbf{Q}_m} \big)
    &=
    \widehat{\sigma}_{\Xi,m}
    \widehat{\mathbf{u}}_{\Xi,m}
    \widehat{\mathbf{v}}_{\Xi,m}'
    +
    \widehat{\Xi}_m^{(\text{rem})},
    \label{eqn: reloading_SVD_hat}
\end{align}
where the remainder $\widehat{\Xi}_m^{(\text{rem})}$ includes the remaining singular components.
Similarly, write the population version of the above as the rank-1 singular value decomposition and the remaining singular components (which are zero due to the following), such that
\begin{align}
    \mathcal{R}\big( \mathbf{K}_m^0 \big)
    &=
    \sigma_{*,m}
    \mathbf{u}_{*,m}
    \mathbf{v}_{*,m}'
    = \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}(\mathbf{Q}_m^*) \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}(\mathbf{J}_m^*)' ,
    \label{eqn: reloading_SVD_pop}
\end{align}
where $\sigma_{*,m}$ denotes the largest singular value of $\mathcal{R}(\mathbf{K}_m^0)$.
By Assumptions~(S1), (L1), and the asymptotic orthogonality of $\mathbf{H}_{Q,m_0}$ and $\mathbf{H}_{J,m_0}$ from Lemma~\ref{lemma: aligned_projected_cores_rot_rate},
the leading singular value of $\mathcal{R}(\mathbf{K}_m^0)$ satisfies $\sigma_{*,m} \asymp_P 1$.
Then by Weyl's inequality, \eqref{eqn: reloading_final_rate},
and recall that $\mathcal{R}(\cdot)$ preserves the Frobenius norm,
\begin{align}
    \big| \widehat{\sigma}_{\Xi,m}
    - \sigma_{*,m} \big|
    &\lesssim_P
    \big\| \mathcal{R}(\widehat{\mathbf{J}_m \otimes \mathbf{Q}_m}) - \mathcal{R}(\mathbf{K}_m^0) \big\|
    \lesssim_P
    \Delta_{K,m}^{1/2} ,
    \label{eqn: reloading_sigma_perturbation}
\end{align}
which then implies $\widehat{\sigma}_{\Xi,m} \asymp_P 1$.
By the Davis--Kahan theorem \citep[Theorem~2]{yu2015useful}, we have
\begin{align*}
    \big\| \widehat{\mathbf{u}}_{\Xi,m} - \mathbf{u}_{*,m} \big\|^2
    &\lesssim_P
    \frac{\big\| \mathcal{R}(\widehat{\mathbf{J}_m \otimes \mathbf{Q}_m}) - \mathcal{R}(\mathbf{K}_m^0) \big\|_F^2}{(\sigma_{*,m} - \sigma_{*,m}^{(2)})^2 } 
    , \quad
    \big\| \widehat{\mathbf{v}}_{\Xi,m} - \mathbf{v}_{*,m} \big\|^2
    \lesssim_P
    \frac{\big\|\mathcal{R}(\widehat{\mathbf{J}_m \otimes \mathbf{Q}_m}) - \mathcal{R}(\mathbf{K}_m^0) \big\|_F^2}{(\sigma_{*,m} - \sigma_{*,m}^{(2)})^2} ,
\end{align*}
where $\sigma_{*,m}^{(2)}$ denotes the second largest singular value of $\mathcal{R}(\mathbf{K}_m^0)$ such that $\sigma_{*,m}^{(2)} =0$ due to \eqref{eqn: reloading_SVD_pop}, and thus $|\sigma_{*,m} - \sigma_{*,m}^{(2)}| \asymp_P 1$.
Then with \eqref{eqn: reloading_sigma_perturbation}, we may conclude
\begin{align}
    \big\| \widehat{\mathbf{u}}_{\Xi,m} - \mathbf{u}_{*,m} \big\|^2
    &\lesssim_P
    \Delta_{K,m} 
    , \quad
    \big\| \widehat{\mathbf{v}}_{\Xi,m} - \mathbf{v}_{*,m} \big\|^2
    \lesssim_P
    \Delta_{K,m} .
    \label{eqn: reloading_singular_vectors_rate}
\end{align}

Recall from Step~3 of Section~\ref{subsec:estimation} that $\textnormal{\textbf{vec}}(\widetilde{\mathbf{Q}}_m) = \widehat{\sigma}_{\Xi,m}^{1/2} \widehat{\mathbf{u}}_{\Xi,m}$ and $\textnormal{\textbf{vec}}(\widetilde{\mathbf{J}}_m) = \widehat{\sigma}_{\Xi,m}^{1/2} \widehat{\mathbf{v}}_{\Xi,m}$.
Similarly, define their population versions $\textnormal{\textbf{vec}}(\mathbf{Q}_m^*) := \sigma_{*,m}^{1/2} \mathbf{u}_{*,m}$ and $\textnormal{\textbf{vec}}(\mathbf{J}_m^*) = \sigma_{*,m}^{1/2} \mathbf{v}_{*,m}$.
Combining \eqref{eqn: reloading_sigma_perturbation} and \eqref{eqn: reloading_singular_vectors_rate}, we obtain
\begin{align}
    &\;\quad
    \big\| \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}(\widetilde{\mathbf{Q}}_m) - \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}(\mathbf{Q}_m^*) \big\|^2
    =
    \big\| \widehat{\sigma}_{\Xi,m}^{1/2} \widehat{\mathbf{u}}_{\Xi,m}
    - \sigma_{*,m}^{1/2} \mathbf{u}_{*,m} \big\|^2 \notag \\
    &\lesssim
    \big| \widehat{\sigma}_{\Xi,m}^{1/2} - \sigma_{*,m}^{1/2} \big|^2
    \big\| \widehat{\mathbf{u}}_{\Xi,m} \big\|^2
    + \sigma_{*,m} \big\| \widehat{\mathbf{u}}_{\Xi,m} - \mathbf{u}_{*,m} \big\|^2 
    =
    O_P\big( \Delta_{K,m} \big),
    \label{eqn: reloading_Q_rate}
\end{align}
and analogously,
\begin{align}
    \big\| \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}(\widetilde{\mathbf{J}}_m) - \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}(\mathbf{J}_m^*) \big\|^2
    =
    O_P\big( \Delta_{K,m} \big).
    \label{eqn: reloading_J_rate}
\end{align}
Thus finally, the re-estimated global loading matrices $\widetilde{\mathbf{Q}}_m$ and $\widetilde{\mathbf{J}}_m$ satisfy
\begin{align}
    \big\| \widetilde{\mathbf{Q}}_m - \mathbf{Q}_m^* \big\|_F^2
    &=
    O_P\big( \Delta_{K,m} \big),
    \quad
    \big\| \widetilde{\mathbf{J}}_m - \mathbf{J}_m^* \big\|_F^2 
    = 
    O_P\big( \Delta_{K,m} \big) ,
    \label{eqn: reloading_final_individual}
\end{align}
where
\[
\mathbf{Q}_m^* := \mathbf{Q}_m \big( \mathbf{Q}_{m_0}' \mathbf{Q}_{m_0} \big)^{-1/2} \mathbf{H}_{Q,m_0}
, \quad
\mathbf{J}_m^* := \mathbf{J}_m \big( \mathbf{J}_{m_0}' \mathbf{J}_{m_0} \big)^{-1/2} \mathbf{H}_{J,m_0} .
\]
This completes the proof of the theorem.
$\square$

By (ME1), we have $\lambda_{r_1}(\mathbf{A}_{1m}'\mathbf{A}_{1m})\asymp\lambda_1(\mathbf{A}_{1m}'\mathbf{A}_{1m})\asymp p_m^{\gamma_r}$. Moreover, since $\mathbf{A}_{1n}'\mathbf{A}_{1n}\succeq0$ for every $n\ne m$,
\begin{align*}
    \lambda_{r_1}\left(\sum_{n\ne m}\mathbf{A}_{1n}'\mathbf{A}_{1n}\right)
    &\geq\sum_{n\ne m}\lambda_{r_1}(\mathbf{A}_{1n}'\mathbf{A}_{1n})
    \asymp\sum_{n\ne m}p_n^{\gamma_r},\\
    \lambda_1\left(\sum_{n\ne m}\mathbf{A}_{1n}'\mathbf{A}_{1n}\right)
    &\leq\sum_{n\ne m}\lambda_1(\mathbf{A}_{1n}'\mathbf{A}_{1n})
    \asymp\sum_{n\ne m}p_n^{\gamma_r}.
\end{align*}
By (S1), $\lambda_{r_1}\left(T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\mathbbm{E}(\boldsymbol{\alpha}_t\boldsymbol{\alpha}_t')\right)\asymp\lambda_1\left(T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\mathbbm{E}(\boldsymbol{\alpha}_t\boldsymbol{\alpha}_t')\right)\asymp1$. Together with the preceding bounds and (ME1), we have
\begin{align*}
    \lambda_{r_1}(\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{A_1,m})\asymp\lambda_1(\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{A_1,m})
    \asymp p_m^{\gamma_r}\sum_{n\ne m}p_n^{\gamma_r}
    =\omega_{A_1,m}.
\end{align*}
By \eqref{eqn:Omega_A1_full_decomposition}, Lemma~\ref{lemma:bound_S_A1_Delta_A1},
\begin{align*}
    \big\| \widehat{\boldsymbol{\Omega}}_{A_1,m}-\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{A_1,m} \big\|_F
    &\lesssim\sum_{n\ne m}\left\{\big\| \boldsymbol{\Delta}_{A_1,mn} \big\|_F\big\| \mathbf{S}_{A_1,mn} \big\|_F+\big\| \boldsymbol{\Delta}_{A_1,mn} \big\|_F^2\right\}\\
    &=o_P\left(p_m^{\gamma_r}\sum_{n\ne m}p_n^{\gamma_r}\right)
    =o_P(\omega_{A_1,m}).
\end{align*}
Therefore, Weyl's inequality gives
\begin{align*}
    \big|\lambda_{r_1}(\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Omega}}_{A_1,m})-\lambda_{r_1}(\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{A_1,m})\big|
    \leq\big\| \widehat{\boldsymbol{\Omega}}_{A_1,m}-\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{A_1,m} \big\|
    \leq\big\| \widehat{\boldsymbol{\Omega}}_{A_1,m}-\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{A_1,m} \big\|_F
    =o_P(\omega_{A_1,m}),
\end{align*}
and hence $\lambda_{r_1}(\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Omega}}_{A_1,m})\asymp_P\omega_{A_1,m}$. Thus, $\widehat{\mathbf{D}}_{A_1,m}$ is invertible with probability tending to one and, by \eqref{eqn:Omega_A1_A1_D1},
\begin{align*}
    \big\| \widehat{\mathbf{D}}_{A_1,m}^{-1} \big\|_F^2
    =\sum_{i=1}^{r_1}\lambda_i^{-2}(\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Omega}}_{A_1,m})
    \lesssim\lambda_{r_1}^{-2}(\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Omega}}_{A_1,m})
    =O_P(\omega_{A_1,m}^{-2}),
\end{align*}
which completes the proof. $\square$

\label{lemma: common_comp_global_local_init}(Properties of $\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{Q,m}$)
For any $m,n\in[M]$ with $n\neq m$, define
\begin{align*}
    & \boldsymbol{\Omega}_{Q,m} := \frac{1}{M-1} \sum_{n=1;n\neq m}^M \mathbf{S}_{Q,mn}^{\otimes 2},
    \;\;\;
    \mathbf{S}_{Q,mn} := \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=1}^T \mathbbm{E}\left( \mathbf{Q}_m\mathbf{G}_t\mathbf{J}_m' \mathbf{v}_b^{(m)} \mathbf{v}_b^{(n)'} \mathbf{J}_n\mathbf{G}_t'\mathbf{Q}_n' \right) \\
    & \widehat{\mathbf{S}}_{Q,mn} := \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=1}^T\widecheck{\mathbf{Y}}_t^{(m)} \mathbf{v}_b^{(m)} \mathbf{v}_b^{(n)'} \widecheck{\mathbf{Y}}_t^{(n)'} ,
    \;\;\;
    \boldsymbol{\Delta}_{Q,mn} := \widehat{\mathbf{S}}_{Q,mn} - \mathbf{S}_{Q,mn} .
\end{align*}
Then under Assumptions~(IC1), (E1), (E2), (F1), and (L1), we have
\begin{align*}
    \| \boldsymbol{\Delta}_{Q,mn} \|_F^2
    &\lesssim_P
    p_m^{\delta_{q,1}^{(m)}} p_n^{\delta_{q,1}^{(n)}} s_{J,m}^2 s_{J,n}^2 R(T,d_{\text{fac},\star})
    + p_m^{\delta_{r,1}^{(m)}} p_n^{\delta_{q,1}^{(n)}} s_{J,n}^2  q_m^{\delta_{c,1}^{(m)}} R(T,d_{\text{fac},\star}) \\
    &\;\quad
    + p_m^{\delta_{q,1}^{(m)}} p_n^{\delta_{r,1}^{(n)}} s_{J,m}^2 q_n^{\delta_{c,1}^{(n)}} R(T,d_{\text{fac},\star}) 
    + p_m^{\delta_{r,1}^{(m)}} p_n^{\delta_{r,1}^{(n)}} q_m^{\delta_{c,1}^{(m)}} q_n^{\delta_{c,1}^{(n)}}  R(T,d_{\text{fac},\star}) 
    + T^{-1} p_m p_n^{\delta_{q,1}^{(n)}} s_{J,n}^2 \\
    &\;\quad
    + T^{-1} p_m p_n^{\delta_{r,1}^{(n)}} q_n^{\delta_{c,1}^{(n)}} 
    + T^{-1} p_m^{\delta_{q,1}^{(m)}} s_{J,m}^2 p_n
    + T^{-1} p_m^{\delta_{r,1}^{(m)}} q_m^{\delta_{c,1}^{(m)}} p_n 
    + T^{-1} p_m p_n .
\end{align*}
Further define $\widecheck{\mathbf{Q}}_m := \mathbf{Q}_m (\mathbf{Q}_m'\mathbf{Q}_m)^{-1/2}$.
Then under Assumptions~(L2) and (R2), there exists an asymptotically orthogonal matrix $\mathbf{H}_{Q,m}$ with $\mathbf{H}_{Q,m} \mathbf{H}_{Q,m}'=\mathbf{I}+o_P(1)$,
such that
\[
\big\| \widehat{\mathbf{Q}}_m - \widecheck{\mathbf{Q}}_m \mathbf{H}_{Q,m} \big\|^2 = O_P\left\{
R(T,d_{\text{fac},\star}) \;
p_m^{2 (\delta_{q,1}^{(m)} -\delta_{q,k_r}^{(m)})}
\left( \frac{  \max_{n\in[M] \setminus \{m\}} s_{J,n}^2 p_n^{\delta_{q,1}^{(n)}}}{\max_{n\in[M] \setminus\{m\}} s_{J,n}^2 p_n^{\delta_{q,k_r}^{(n)}}} \right)^2
\right\} .
\]
Analogous results hold for $\widehat{\mathbf{J}}_m$, with asymptotically orthogonal matrix $\mathbf{H}_{J,m}$.
