body_md:
By Assumption~(F1), we note that $T^{-1} \sum_{t=1}^T \mathbbm{E}[\mathbf{z}_{G,t}^{\otimes 2}]$ and $T^{-1} \sum_{t=1}^T \mathbbm{E}[(\mathbf{z}_{F,t}^{(m)})^{\otimes 2}]$ are diagonal due to the independence between cross-sectional entries. Without loss of generality, we further normalize these long-run covariance matrices to be the identity matrix. Namely, we will assume throughout the proof that
\begin{equation}
\label{eqn: long_run_cov_vec_fac}
\frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=1}^T \mathbbm{E}[\mathbf{z}_{G,t}^{\otimes 2}] = \mathbf{I}_{k_rk_c} , \;\;\;
\frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=1}^T \mathbbm{E}[(\mathbf{z}_{F,t}^{(m)})^{\otimes 2}] = \mathbf{I}_{k_r^{(m)} k_c^{(m)}} .
\end{equation}
This is equivalent to absorbing the entry-wise variance into $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{Q,m}$, $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{J,m}$, $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{R,m}$ and $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{C,m}$ (from Assumption~(L1)) which are arbitrary positive-definite matrices with eigenvalues uniformly bounded away from 0 and infinity.
Then for any group $m\in[M]$, by definitions we have
\begin{align}
    &\;\quad
    \widecheck{\mathbf{Y}}_t^{(m)} = \mathbf{Y}_t^{(m)} - \widehat{c}_t^{(m)}\1
    _{p_m}\1_{q_m}' - \widehat{\mathbf{a}}_t^{(m)}\1_{q_m}' - \1_{p_m}\widehat{\mathbf{b}}_t^{(m)'} \notag \\
    &=
    \mathbf{Y}_t^{(m)} - (p_mq_m)^{-1} \1_{p_m} \1_{p_m}' \mathbf{Y}_t^{(m)}\1_{q_m}\1_{q_m}' - q_m^{-1} \mathbf{M}_{p_m}\mathbf{Y}_t^{(m)}\1_{q_m} \1_{q_m}' - p_m^{-1} \1_{p_m} \1_{p_m}' \mathbf{Y}_t^{(m)} \mathbf{M}_{q_m} \notag \\
    &=
    \mathbf{M}_{p_m} \mathbf{Y}_t^{(m)} \mathbf{M}_{q_m} + p_m^{-1} \1_{p_m} \1_{p_m}' \mathbf{Y}_t^{(m)} \mathbf{M}_{q_m} + q_m^{-1} \mathbf{Y}_t^{(m)} \1_{q_m} \1_{q_m}' 
    - (p_mq_m)^{-1} \1_{p_m} \1_{p_m}' \mathbf{Y}_t^{(m)}\1_{q_m}\1_{q_m}'  \notag \\
    &\;\quad
    - q_m^{-1} \mathbf{M}_{p_m} \mathbf{Y}_t^{(m)} \1_{q_m} \1_{q_m}' - p_m^{-1} \1_{p_m} \1_{p_m}' \mathbf{Y}_t^{(m)} \mathbf{M}_{q_m}
    = \mathbf{M}_{p_m} \mathbf{Y}_t^{(m)} \mathbf{M}_{q_m} . \notag
\end{align}
Together with our model \eqref{eqn:MMEFM}, Assumption~(IC1), and the fact that $\mathbf{M}_a \1_a =\0$ for any positive integer $a$, we further arrive at
\begin{align}
    \widecheck{\mathbf{Y}}_t^{(m)} &= \mathbf{M}_{p_m} \mathbf{Y}_t^{(m)} \mathbf{M}_{q_m} =
    \mathbf{M}_{p_m} \mathbf{Q}_m\mathbf{G}_t\mathbf{J}_m' \mathbf{M}_{q_m}
    + \mathbf{M}_{p_m} \mathbf{R}_m\mathbf{F}_t^{(m)}\mathbf{C}_m'  \mathbf{M}_{q_m}
    + \mathbf{M}_{p_m} \mathbf{E}_t^{(m)} \mathbf{M}_{q_m}  \notag \\
    &=
    \mathbf{Q}_m\mathbf{G}_t\mathbf{J}_m'
    + \mathbf{R}_m\mathbf{F}_t^{(m)}\mathbf{C}_m' 
    + \mathbf{M}_{p_m} \mathbf{E}_t^{(m)} \mathbf{M}_{q_m} .
    \label{eqn: check_Yt_m_simplify}
\end{align}

Then it holds that
\begin{align}
    &\;\quad
    \widehat{\mathbf{S}}_{Q,mn} \notag \\
    &= 
    \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=1}^T \Big( \mathbf{Q}_m\mathbf{G}_t\mathbf{J}_m' \mathbf{v}_b^{(m)} + \mathbf{R}_m\mathbf{F}_t^{(m)}\mathbf{C}_m' \mathbf{v}_b^{(m)} + \mathbf{M}_{p_m} \mathbf{E}_t^{(m)} \mathbf{M}_{q_m} \mathbf{v}_b^{(m)} \Big) \notag \\
    &\;\quad
    \cdot \Big( \mathbf{v}_b^{(n)'} \mathbf{J}_n\mathbf{G}_t'\mathbf{Q}_n'  + \mathbf{v}_b^{(n)'} \mathbf{C}_n\mathbf{F}_t^{(n)'} \mathbf{R}_n' + \mathbf{v}_b^{(n)'} \mathbf{M}_{q_n} \mathbf{E}_t^{(n)'} \mathbf{M}_{p_n} \Big) \notag \\
    &=
    \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=1}^T \mathbf{Q}_m\mathbf{G}_t\mathbf{J}_m' \mathbf{v}_b^{(m)} \mathbf{v}_b^{(n)'} \mathbf{J}_n\mathbf{G}_t'\mathbf{Q}_n'
    + \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=1}^T \mathbf{R}_m\mathbf{F}_t^{(m)}\mathbf{C}_m' \mathbf{v}_b^{(m)} \mathbf{v}_b^{(n)'} \mathbf{J}_n\mathbf{G}_t'\mathbf{Q}_n' \notag \\
    &\;\quad
    + \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=1}^T \mathbf{M}_{p_m} \mathbf{E}_t^{(m)} \mathbf{M}_{q_m} \mathbf{v}_b^{(m)} \mathbf{v}_b^{(n)'} \mathbf{J}_n\mathbf{G}_t'\mathbf{Q}_n'
    + \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=1}^T \mathbf{Q}_m\mathbf{G}_t\mathbf{J}_m' \mathbf{v}_b^{(m)} \mathbf{v}_b^{(n)'} \mathbf{C}_n\mathbf{F}_t^{(n)'} \mathbf{R}_n'  \notag \\
    &\;\quad
    + \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=1}^T \mathbf{R}_m\mathbf{F}_t^{(m)}\mathbf{C}_m' \mathbf{v}_b^{(m)} \mathbf{v}_b^{(n)'} \mathbf{C}_n\mathbf{F}_t^{(n)'} \mathbf{R}_n' 
    + \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=1}^T \mathbf{M}_{p_m} \mathbf{E}_t^{(m)} \mathbf{M}_{q_m} \mathbf{v}_b^{(m)} \mathbf{v}_b^{(n)'} \mathbf{C}_n\mathbf{F}_t^{(n)'} \mathbf{R}_n' \notag \\
    &\;\quad 
    + \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=1}^T \mathbf{Q}_m\mathbf{G}_t\mathbf{J}_m' \mathbf{v}_b^{(m)} \mathbf{v}_b^{(n)'} \mathbf{M}_{q_n} \mathbf{E}_t^{(n)'} \mathbf{M}_{p_n}  
    + \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=1}^T \mathbf{R}_m\mathbf{F}_t^{(m)}\mathbf{C}_m' \mathbf{v}_b^{(m)} \mathbf{v}_b^{(n)'} \mathbf{M}_{q_n} \mathbf{E}_t^{(n)'} \mathbf{M}_{p_n} \notag \\
    &\;\quad
    + \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=1}^T \mathbf{M}_{p_m} \mathbf{E}_t^{(m)} \mathbf{M}_{q_m} \mathbf{v}_b^{(m)} \mathbf{v}_b^{(n)'} \mathbf{M}_{q_n} \mathbf{E}_t^{(n)'} \mathbf{M}_{p_n} \notag \\
    &=:
    \mathcal{I}_{Q,mn} + \mathcal{II}_{Q,mn} + \mathcal{III}_{Q,mn} + \mathcal{IV}_{Q,mn} + \mathcal{V}_{Q,mn} + \mathcal{VI}_{Q,mn} + \mathcal{VII}_{Q,mn} + \mathcal{VIII}_{Q,mn} + \mathcal{IX}_{Q,mn} .
    \label{eqn: decomp_hat_S_Q_mn}
\end{align}


Consider first $\mathcal{I}_{Q,mn} - \mathbf{S}_{Q,mn}$.
Define $\mathbf{z}_{G,t} := \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}(\mathbf{G}_t)$ for any $t\in[T]$.
As the dimensions of $\mathbf{G}_t$ are bounded, Lemma~\ref{lemma:prop_piecewise} implies that
\begin{equation}
\label{eqn: GG_var}
\left\| \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=1}^T \left\{ \mathbf{z}_{G,t} \mathbf{z}_{G,t}' - \mathbbm{E}\big[ \mathbf{z}_{G,t} \mathbf{z}_{G,t}' \big] \right\} \right\|_F^2
= O_P(R(T,d_{\text{fac},\star})) ,
\end{equation}
where $R(\cdot, \cdot)$ is defined in \eqref{eqn:R(T,d)} and $d_{\text{fac},\star}$ is the largest long-memory exponent among all processes in $\{\mathbf{G}_t\}$ and $\{\mathbf{F}_t^{(m)}\}$ for $m\in[M]$.
Then from Assumption~(L1), by the triangle inequality we have
\begin{align}
    &\;\quad
    \Big\| \mathcal{I}_{Q,mn} - \mathbf{S}_{Q,mn} \Big\|_F^2 = 
    \left\| \mathbf{Q}_m \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=1}^T \left(  \mathbf{G}_t\mathbf{J}_m' \mathbf{v}_b^{(m)} \mathbf{v}_b^{(n)'} \mathbf{J}_n\mathbf{G}_t' - \mathbbm{E}\left[ \mathbf{G}_t\mathbf{J}_m' \mathbf{v}_b^{(m)} \mathbf{v}_b^{(n)'} \mathbf{J}_n\mathbf{G}_t' \right] \right) \mathbf{Q}_n' \right\|_F^2 \notag \\
    &\lesssim
    \frac{1}{T^2} \cdot p_m^{\delta_{q,1}^{(m)}} \cdot p_n^{\delta_{q,1}^{(n)}} \cdot \left\| \sum_{t=1}^T \left(  \mathbf{G}_t\mathbf{J}_m' \mathbf{v}_b^{(m)} \mathbf{v}_b^{(n)'} \mathbf{J}_n\mathbf{G}_t' - \mathbbm{E}\left[ \mathbf{G}_t\mathbf{J}_m' \mathbf{v}_b^{(m)} \mathbf{v}_b^{(n)'} \mathbf{J}_n\mathbf{G}_t' \right] \right) \right\|_F^2 \notag \\
    &=
    \frac{1}{T^2} \cdot p_m^{\delta_{q,1}^{(m)}} \cdot p_n^{\delta_{q,1}^{(n)}} \cdot \left\| \sum_{t=1}^T \left\{ (\mathbf{G}_t \otimes \mathbf{G}_t) \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}(\mathbf{J}_m' \mathbf{v}_b^{(m)} \mathbf{v}_b^{(n)'} \mathbf{J}_n) - \mathbbm{E}\left[ (\mathbf{G}_t \otimes \mathbf{G}_t) \textnormal{\textbf{vec}}(\mathbf{J}_m' \mathbf{v}_b^{(m)} \mathbf{v}_b^{(n)'} \mathbf{J}_n) \right] \right\} \right\|_F^2 \notag \\
    &\leq
    \frac{1}{T^2} \cdot p_m^{\delta_{q,1}^{(m)}} \cdot p_n^{\delta_{q,1}^{(n)}} \cdot \left\| \sum_{t=1}^T \left\{ \mathbf{G}_t \otimes \mathbf{G}_t - \mathbbm{E}[\mathbf{G}_t \otimes \mathbf{G}_t] \right\} \right\|_F^2
    \cdot \left\| \mathbf{J}_m' \mathbf{v}_b^{(m)} \mathbf{v}_b^{(n)'} \mathbf{J}_n \right\|_F^2 \notag \\
    &\asymp
    p_m^{\delta_{q,1}^{(m)}} \cdot p_n^{\delta_{q,1}^{(n)}} \cdot \left\| \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=1}^T \left\{ \mathbf{z}_{G,t} \mathbf{z}_{G,t}' - \mathbbm{E}\big[ \mathbf{z}_{G,t} \mathbf{z}_{G,t}' \big] \right\} \right\|_F^2
    \cdot \left\| \mathbf{J}_m' \mathbf{v}_b^{(m)} \mathbf{v}_b^{(n)'} \mathbf{J}_n \right\|_F^2 \notag \\
    &\lesssim_P
    p_m^{\delta_{q,1}^{(m)}} \cdot p_n^{\delta_{q,1}^{(n)}} \cdot
    R(T,d_{\text{fac},\star}) \cdot \left\| \mathbf{J}_m' \mathbf{v}_b^{(m)} \mathbf{v}_b^{(n)'} \mathbf{J}_n \right\|_F^2 \notag \\
    &\lesssim_P
    p_m^{\delta_{q,1}^{(m)}} \cdot p_n^{\delta_{q,1}^{(n)}} \cdot
    s_{J,m}^2 \cdot s_{J,n}^2 \cdot
    R(T,d_{\text{fac},\star}) ,
    \label{eqn: cI_Q_mn}
\end{align}
where the first equivalence follows from the fact that the Frobenius norm of $\mathbf{G}_t \otimes \mathbf{G}_t$ equals that of $\mathbf{z}_{G,t} \mathbf{z}_{G,t}'$ under a fixed permutation of their entries, the second last inequality used \eqref{eqn: GG_var}, 
and the last used the definitions of $s_{J,m}$ and $s_{J,n}$.

By Assumption~(L1), analogous arguments in \eqref{eqn: cI_Q_mn},
and the fact $\mathbf{v}_b^{(m)}$ and $\mathbf{v}_b^{(n)}$ are unit vectors by construction,
we may also obtain
\begin{align}
    \|\mathcal{II}_{Q,mn}\|_F^2 &
    \lesssim_P
    p_m^{\delta_{r,1}^{(m)}} \cdot p_n^{\delta_{q,1}^{(n)}} \cdot
    s_{J,n}^2 \cdot q_m^{\delta_{c,1}^{(m)}} \cdot
    R(T,d_{\text{fac},\star}) , \label{eqn: cII_Q_mn} \\
    \|\mathcal{IV}_{Q,mn}\|_F^2 &
    \lesssim_P
    p_m^{\delta_{q,1}^{(m)}} \cdot p_n^{\delta_{r,1}^{(n)}} \cdot
    s_{J,m}^2 \cdot q_n^{\delta_{c,1}^{(n)}} \cdot
    R(T,d_{\text{fac},\star}) , \label{eqn: cIV_Q_mn} \\
    \|\mathcal{V}_{Q,mn}\|_F^2 &
    \lesssim_P
    p_m^{\delta_{r,1}^{(m)}} \cdot p_n^{\delta_{r,1}^{(n)}} \cdot
    q_m^{\delta_{c,1}^{(m)}} \cdot q_n^{\delta_{c,1}^{(n)}} \cdot
    R(T,d_{\text{fac},\star}) . \label{eqn: cV_Q_mn} 
\end{align}

We next bound the noise-involved terms in \eqref{eqn: decomp_hat_S_Q_mn}, i.e., $\mathcal{III}_{Q,mn}$, $\mathcal{VI}_{Q,mn}$, $\mathcal{VII}_{Q,mn}$, $\mathcal{VIII}_{Q,mn}$, and $\mathcal{IX}_{Q,mn}$.
For each $m\in[M]$, define $a_{m} := \mathbf{M}_{q_m} \mathbf{v}_b^{(m)}$ and $b_{m} := \mathbf{J}_m' \mathbf{v}_b^{(m)}$.
By construction, $\|a_{m}\| \leq 1$ and $\|b_{m}\| = s_{J,m}$. 
We first present a simple but useful bound. For any deterministic vector $a\in\mathbb{R}^{q_m}$ with $\|a\|\leq 1$, Lemma~\ref{lemma:correlation_Etm} implies that, uniformly in $t$,
\begin{align}
    \mathbbm{E}\big\| \mathbf{M}_{p_m} \mathbf{E}_t^{(m)} a \big\|^2 
    = O(p_m) ,
    \label{eqn: unit_vector_error_bound}
\end{align}
which used that for each row $i\in[p_m]$, the covariance matrix of the row vector $(\mathbf{E}_t^{(m)})_{i\cdot}$ has row-wise $\ell_1$-norms bounded by a constant under Lemma~\ref{lemma:correlation_Etm},
and as the covariance matrix is symmetric and positive semidefinite, its spectral norm is bounded by the same constant, and thus the above bound follows by summing over $i\in[p_m]$.
Also, by Assumptions~(F1) and (L1), we have
\begin{align}
    \mathbbm{E}\big\| \mathbf{Q}_n \mathbf{G}_t b_n \big\|^{2}
    \lesssim
    p_n^{\delta_{q,1}^{(n)}} s_{J,n}^2 , \qquad
    \mathbbm{E}\big\| \mathbf{R}_n \mathbf{F}_t^{(n)} \mathbf{C}_n' \mathbf{v}_b^{(n)} \big\|^2
    \lesssim
    p_n^{\delta_{r,1}^{(n)}} q_n^{\delta_{c,1}^{(n)}} .
    \label{eqn: factor_vector_second_moments}
\end{align}


Consider $\mathcal{III}_{Q,mn}$. For neatness, define $u_{n,t} := \mathbf{Q}_n \mathbf{G}_t b_n $ and $e_{m,t} := \mathbf{M}_{p_m} \mathbf{E}_t^{(m)} a_m$. Then we can write $\mathcal{III}_{Q,mn} = T^{-1} \sum_{t=1}^{T} e_{m,t} u_{n,t}'$.
By Assumption~(E2), the processes $\{e_{m,t}\}_{t\in[T]}$ and $\{u_{n,t}\}_{t\in[T]}$ are independent. Hence we have
\begin{align}
    \mathbbm{E}\big\| \mathcal{III}_{Q,mn} \big\|_F^2
    &=
    \frac{1}{T^2}
    \sum_{t=1}^{T}
    \sum_{s=1}^{T}
    \mathbbm{E}\Big( u_{n,t}' u_{n,s} \Big)
    \mathbbm{E}\Big( e_{m,t}' e_{m,s} \Big) .
    \label{eqn: cIII_expansion}
\end{align}
We bound the two expectations on the right-hand side separately. First, by the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality and \eqref{eqn: factor_vector_second_moments}, we have
\begin{align}
    \Big| \mathbbm{E}\Big( u_{n,t}' u_{n,s} \Big) \Big|
    &\leq
    \Big( \mathbbm{E}\big\| u_{n,t} \big\|^{2} \Big)^{1/2}
    \Big( \mathbbm{E}\big\| u_{n,s} \big\|^{2} \Big)^{1/2} 
    \lesssim
    p_n^{\delta_{q,1}^{(n)}} s_{J,n}^2 .
    \label{eqn: cIII_factor_expectation_bound}
\end{align}
Second, by the lagged version of \eqref{eqn: unit_vector_error_bound}, for any $t,s \in[T]$,
\begin{align}
    \Big| \mathbbm{E}\Big( e_{m,t}' e_{m,s} \Big) \Big|
    \lesssim
    p_m \rho(|t-s|) ,
    \label{eqn: cIII_error_expectation_bound}
\end{align}
where $\rho(\cdot)$ is the summable sequence from Lemma~\ref{lemma:correlation_Etm}.
Substituting \eqref{eqn: cIII_factor_expectation_bound} and \eqref{eqn: cIII_error_expectation_bound} into \eqref{eqn: cIII_expansion} gives
\begin{align}
    \mathbbm{E}\big\| \mathcal{III}_{Q,mn} \big\|_F^2
    &\lesssim
    T^{-2} p_m p_n^{\delta_{q,1}^{(n)}} s_{J,n}^{2}
    \sum_{t=1}^{T} \sum_{s=1}^{T} \rho(|t-s|) \notag \\
    &\lesssim
    T^{-2} \cdot p_m p_n^{\delta_{q,1}^{(n)}} s_{J,n}^{2} \cdot T
    =
    T^{-1} p_m p_n^{\delta_{q,1}^{(n)}} s_{J,n}^{2} ,
    \label{eqn: cIII_Q_mn}
\end{align}
where the second line follows from evaluating the double sum, viz.\ setting $h = t-s$ gives
\begin{align*}
    \sum_{t=1}^{T} \sum_{s=1}^{T} \rho(|t-s|)
    &=
    \sum_{h= -(T-1)}^{T-1} (T-|h|) \rho(|h|)
    \leq
    T \sum_{h= -\infty}^{\infty} \rho(|h|)
    = O(T) ,
\end{align*}
where the final equality follows from the summability of $\rho(\cdot)$ as in Lemma~\ref{lemma:correlation_Etm}. 
We mark that \eqref{eqn: cIII_Q_mn} carries $T^{-1}$ rather than $R(T,d_{\text{fac},\star})$ as in e.g.\ \eqref{eqn: cI_Q_mn}, since here we consider the cross-moment between the factor and noise processes, whereas previously, say \eqref{eqn: cI_Q_mn}, the sample covariance of factor processes is considered.


The same arguments can be applied to $\mathcal{VI}_{Q,mn}$, $\mathcal{VII}_{Q,mn}$, $\mathcal{VIII}_{Q,mn}$ and $\mathcal{IX}_{Q,mn}$, yielding
\begin{align}
    \big\| \mathcal{VI}_{Q,mn} \big\|_F^2
    &=
    O_P\Big( T^{-1} p_m p_n^{\delta_{r,1}^{(n)}} q_n^{\delta_{c,1}^{(n)}} \Big) ,
    \label{eqn: cVI_Q_mn} \\
    \big\| \mathcal{VII}_{Q,mn} \big\|_F^2
    &=
    O_P\Big( T^{-1} p_m^{\delta_{q,1}^{(m)}} s_{J,m}^2 p_n \Big) ,
    \label{eqn: cVII_Q_mn} \\
    \big\| \mathcal{VIII}_{Q,mn} \big\|_F^2
    &=
    O_P\Big( T^{-1} p_m^{\delta_{r,1}^{(m)}} q_m^{\delta_{c,1}^{(m)}} p_n \Big) , 
    \label{eqn: cVIII_Q_mn} \\
    \big\| \mathcal{IX}_{Q,mn} \big\|_F^2
    &=
    O_P\Big( T^{-1} p_m p_n \Big) ,
    \label{eqn: cIX_Q_mn}
\end{align}
where in each case, the bound follows by separating the independent vector processes, applying \eqref{eqn: unit_vector_error_bound} to the error part, \eqref{eqn: factor_vector_second_moments} to the factor part, and using the short-memory property of the error process to sum over $t,s$.
Lastly, combining \eqref{eqn: decomp_hat_S_Q_mn}, 
\eqref{eqn: cI_Q_mn},
\eqref{eqn: cII_Q_mn},
\eqref{eqn: cIII_Q_mn},
\eqref{eqn: cIV_Q_mn},
\eqref{eqn: cV_Q_mn},
\eqref{eqn: cVI_Q_mn},
\eqref{eqn: cVII_Q_mn},
\eqref{eqn: cVIII_Q_mn},
and \eqref{eqn: cIX_Q_mn},
together with the definitions of $\boldsymbol{\Delta}_{Q,mn}$, we may conclude that
\begin{align*}
    &\;\quad
    \|\boldsymbol{\Delta}_{Q,mn} \|_F^2 
    =  \| \widehat{\mathbf{S}}_{Q,mn} - \mathbf{S}_{Q,mn} \|_F^2 \\
    &\lesssim
    \Big\| \mathcal{I}_{Q,mn} - \mathbf{S}_{Q,mn} \Big\|_F^2
    + \big\| \mathcal{II}_{Q,mn} \big\|_F^2
    + \big\| \mathcal{III}_{Q,mn} \big\|_F^2
    + \big\| \mathcal{IV}_{Q,mn} \big\|_F^2
    + \big\| \mathcal{V}_{Q,mn} \big\|_F^2 \\
    &\;\quad
    + \big\| \mathcal{VI}_{Q,mn} \big\|_F^2
    + \big\| \mathcal{VII}_{Q,mn} \big\|_F^2
    + \big\| \mathcal{VIII}_{Q,mn} \big\|_F^2
    + \big\| \mathcal{IX}_{Q,mn} \big\|_F^2 \\
    &\lesssim_P
    p_m^{\delta_{q,1}^{(m)}} p_n^{\delta_{q,1}^{(n)}} s_{J,m}^2 s_{J,n}^2 R(T,d_{\text{fac},\star})
    + p_m^{\delta_{r,1}^{(m)}} p_n^{\delta_{q,1}^{(n)}} s_{J,n}^2  q_m^{\delta_{c,1}^{(m)}} R(T,d_{\text{fac},\star}) 
    + p_m^{\delta_{q,1}^{(m)}} p_n^{\delta_{r,1}^{(n)}} s_{J,m}^2 q_n^{\delta_{c,1}^{(n)}} R(T,d_{\text{fac},\star}) \\
    &\;\quad
    + p_m^{\delta_{r,1}^{(m)}} p_n^{\delta_{r,1}^{(n)}} q_m^{\delta_{c,1}^{(m)}} q_n^{\delta_{c,1}^{(n)}}  R(T,d_{\text{fac},\star}) 
    + T^{-1} p_m p_n^{\delta_{q,1}^{(n)}} s_{J,n}^2
    + T^{-1} p_m p_n^{\delta_{r,1}^{(n)}} q_n^{\delta_{c,1}^{(n)}} \\
    &\;\quad
    + T^{-1} p_m^{\delta_{q,1}^{(m)}} s_{J,m}^2 p_n
    + T^{-1} p_m^{\delta_{r,1}^{(m)}} q_m^{\delta_{c,1}^{(m)}} p_n 
    + T^{-1} p_m p_n .
\end{align*}
This completes the proof on $\| \boldsymbol{\Delta}_{Q,mn} \|_F^2$.



Next, we focus on the $k_r$-th eigenvalue of $\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{Q,m}$.
First, by Assumption~(F1), for any $m,n\in[M]$, we may simplify and write
\begin{align}
    \mathbf{S}_{Q,mn} &= \mathbf{Q}_m \mathbbm{E}\left( \mathbf{G}_t\mathbf{J}_m' \mathbf{v}_b^{(m)} \mathbf{v}_b^{(n)'} \mathbf{J}_n\mathbf{G}_t' \right) \mathbf{Q}_n' \notag \\
    &=
    \text{tr}\left( \mathbf{J}_m' \mathbf{v}_b^{(m)} \mathbf{v}_b^{(n)'} \mathbf{J}_n \right) \mathbf{Q}_m \mathbf{Q}_n'
    =
    \left( \mathbf{v}_b^{(n)'} \mathbf{J}_n \mathbf{J}_m' \mathbf{v}_b^{(m)} \right) \mathbf{Q}_m \mathbf{Q}_n' 
    =:
    w_{mn} \mathbf{Q}_m \mathbf{Q}_n' ,
    \label{eqn: S_Q_mn_simplify}
\end{align}
where by Assumption~(L2), the selected projection directions satisfy
\begin{align}
    |w_{mn}| \asymp s_{J,m}s_{J,n}
    \label{eqn: w_mn_order}
\end{align}
for all $m,n\in[M]$ with $n\neq m$. 
Hence we have $\mathbf{S}_{Q,mn}$ of rank $k_r$, and
\begin{equation}
\label{eqn: S_Q_mn_bound}
\|\mathbf{S}_{Q,mn}\| \asymp_P \Big( s_{J,m}s_{J,n} p_m^{\delta_{q,1}^{(m)} /2} p_n^{\delta_{q,1}^{(n)} /2} \Big) .
\end{equation}
Now plugging \eqref{eqn: S_Q_mn_simplify} in $\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{Q,m}$, we have
\begin{align}
    \boldsymbol{\Omega}_{Q,m} &= 
    \frac{1}{M-1} \sum_{n=1;n\neq m}^M w_{mn}^2 \mathbf{Q}_m \mathbf{Q}_n' \mathbf{Q}_n \mathbf{Q}_m' \notag \\
    &=
    \mathbf{Q}_m \left\{ \frac{1}{M-1} \sum_{n=1;n\neq m}^M w_{mn}^2 \mathbf{Q}_n' \mathbf{Q}_n \right\} \mathbf{Q}_m' 
    =:
    \mathbf{Q}_m \mathbf{G}_{Q,m} \mathbf{Q}_m' .
    \label{eqn: Omega_Q_m_simplify}
\end{align}
We next derive the order of the $k_r$-th eigenvalue of $\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{Q,m}$.
For any nonzero vector $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbbm{R}^{k_r}$,
\begin{align}
    \mathbf{x}'\mathbf{G}_{Q,m}\mathbf{x}
    &=
    \frac{1}{M-1} \sum_{n=1;n\neq m}^{M} w_{mn}^{2} \mathbf{x}'\mathbf{Q}_n'\mathbf{Q}_n\mathbf{x}
    =
    \frac{1}{M-1} \sum_{n=1;n\neq m}^{M} w_{mn}^{2} \|\mathbf{Q}_n\mathbf{x}\|^{2}
    \notag \\
    &\ge
    \frac{1}{M-1} \sum_{n=1;n\neq m}^{M} w_{mn}^{2} \lambda_{\min}(\mathbf{Q}_n'\mathbf{Q}_n) \|\mathbf{x}\|^{2} .
    \label{eqn: G_Q_m_lower_rayleigh}
\end{align}
By Assumption~(L1), $\lambda_{\min}(\mathbf{Q}_n'\mathbf{Q}_n) \asymp p_n^{\delta_{q,k_r}^{(n)}}$ for each $n\in[M]$. Combining this with \eqref{eqn: w_mn_order} and \eqref{eqn: G_Q_m_lower_rayleigh} gives
\begin{align}
    \lambda_{\min}(\mathbf{G}_{Q,m})
    \gtrsim
    \frac{s_{J,m}^{2}}{M-1}
    \sum_{n=1;n\neq m}^{M} s_{J,n}^{2} p_n^{\delta_{q,k_r}^{(n)}} 
    \asymp
    s_{J,m}^{2} \max_{n\in[M] \setminus\{m\}} s_{J,n}^{2} p_n^{\delta_{q,k_r}^{(n)}} ,
    \label{eqn: lambda_min_G_Q_m}
\end{align}
where also used that $M$ is fixed.
As the right-hand side of \eqref{eqn: lambda_min_G_Q_m} is bounded away from zero, the matrix $\mathbf{G}_{Q,m}$ is positive definite with all eigenvalues bounded away from zero.
Then from \eqref{eqn: Omega_Q_m_simplify},
the nonzero eigenvalues of $\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{Q,m}$ are the same as those of
$\mathbf{G}_{Q,m}^{1/2} \mathbf{Q}_m'\mathbf{Q}_m \mathbf{G}_{Q,m}^{1/2}$. Therefore, we may conclude that
\begin{align}
    \lambda_{k_r}(\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{Q,m})
    &\geq
    \lambda_{\min}(\mathbf{G}_{Q,m}) \lambda_{\min}(\mathbf{Q}_m'\mathbf{Q}_m)
    \asymp
    \lambda_{\min}(\mathbf{G}_{Q,m}) p_m^{\delta_{q,k_r}^{(m)}} 
    \gtrsim
    p_m^{\delta_{q,k_r}^{(m)}} 
    s_{J,m}^{2} \max_{n\in[M] \setminus\{m\}} s_{J,n}^{2} p_n^{\delta_{q,k_r}^{(n)}} ,
    \label{eqn: Omega_Q_m_krth_eigenvalue_lower}
\end{align}
by Assumption~(L1) and \eqref{eqn: lambda_min_G_Q_m},
which particularly implies $\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{Q,m}$ has rank $k_r$.


Next, note that by Assumption~(R2), we may further simplify $\| \boldsymbol{\Delta}_{Q,mn} \|_F^2$ as
\begin{align*}
    \|\boldsymbol{\Delta}_{Q,mn}\|_F^2 
    &= 
    O_P\Big( R(T,d_{\text{fac},\star}) p_m^{\delta_{q,1}^{(m)}} p_n^{\delta_{q,1}^{(n)}} s_{J,m}^2 s_{J,n}^2 \Big)
    = 
    O_P\Big( R(T,d_{\text{fac},\star}) \, \|\mathbf{S}_{Q,mn}\|_F^2 \Big) ,
\end{align*}
where the last equality used \eqref{eqn: S_Q_mn_bound}.
Hence by \eqref{eqn:X_A} and the triangle inequality,
\begin{align*}
    &\;\quad
    \Big\| \mathbf{X}_{Q,m} - \boldsymbol{\Omega}_{Q,m} \Big\| = \left\| \frac{1}{T^2 (M-1)} \sum_{n=1;n\neq m}^M \left\{ \sum_{t=1}^T\widecheck{\mathbf{Y}}_t^{(m)} \mathbf{v}_b^{(m)} \mathbf{v}_b^{(n)'} \widecheck{\mathbf{Y}}_t^{(n)'} \right\}^{\otimes 2} - \boldsymbol{\Omega}_{Q,m} \right\| \\
    &=
    \left\| \left(\frac{1}{M-1} \sum_{n=1;n\neq m}^M \widehat{\mathbf{S}}_{Q,mn}^{\otimes 2} \right) - \boldsymbol{\Omega}_{Q,m} \right\| 
    \leq
    \frac{1}{M-1} \sum_{n=1;n\neq m}^M \left\| \widehat{\mathbf{S}}_{Q,mn} \widehat{\mathbf{S}}_{Q,mn}' - \mathbf{S}_{Q,mn} \mathbf{S}_{Q,mn}' \right\| \\
    &\leq
    \frac{1}{M-1} \sum_{n=1;n\neq m}^M \left\| \boldsymbol{\Delta}_{Q,mn} \widehat{\mathbf{S}}_{Q,mn}' + \mathbf{S}_{Q,mn} \boldsymbol{\Delta}_{Q,mn}' \right\| \\
    &=
    \frac{1}{M-1} \sum_{n=1;n\neq m}^M \left\| \boldsymbol{\Delta}_{Q,mn} \boldsymbol{\Delta}_{Q,mn}' 
    + \boldsymbol{\Delta}_{Q,mn} \mathbf{S}_{Q,mn}'
    + \mathbf{S}_{Q,mn} \boldsymbol{\Delta}_{Q,mn}' \right\| \\
    &\lesssim
    \max_{n\in[M] \setminus \{m\}} \left( \|\boldsymbol{\Delta}_{Q,mn}\|^2 + \|\mathbf{S}_{Q,mn}\| \|\boldsymbol{\Delta}_{Q,mn}\| \right) \\
    &\lesssim
    R(T,d_{\text{fac},\star})^{1/2} \max_{n\in[M] \setminus \{m\}}  \|\mathbf{S}_{Q,mn}\|_F^2
    \asymp
    R(T,d_{\text{fac},\star})^{1/2}
    p_m^{\delta_{q,1}^{(m)}} s_{J,m}^2 
    \max_{n\in[M] \setminus \{m\}}
    s_{J,n}^2 p_n^{\delta_{q,1}^{(n)}} ,
\end{align*}
which, combined with \eqref{eqn: Omega_Q_m_krth_eigenvalue_lower}, applying the Davis--Kahan theorem \citep[Theorem~2]{yu2015useful} gives the desired result on $\widehat{\mathbf{Q}}_m$, and thus concludes this proof.
$\square$

Fix any $m\in[M]$.
Recall $\widecheck{\mathbf{Q}}_m = \mathbf{Q}_m (\mathbf{Q}_m'\mathbf{Q}_m)^{-1/2}$ from Lemma~\ref{lemma: common_comp_global_local_init}, and similarly let $\widecheck{\mathbf{J}}_m := \mathbf{J}_m (\mathbf{J}_m'\mathbf{J}_m)^{-1/2}$. 
Also, recall $\mathbf{H}_{Q,m}$ and $\mathbf{H}_{J,m}$ from Lemma~\ref{lemma: common_comp_global_local_init}. 
For each $m\in[M]$, with
$\widecheck{\mathbf{Y}}_{G,t}^{(m)} = \widecheck{\mathbf{Y}}_t^{(m)} - \widehat{\mathbf{R}}_m\widehat{\mathbf{F}}_t^{(m)} \widehat{\mathbf{C}}_m'$ from Step~3 of Section~\ref{subsec:estimation},
define
\[
\widecheck{\mathbf{G}}_{t,m} := \widecheck{\mathbf{Q}}_m' \mathbf{Q}_m \mathbf{G}_t\mathbf{J}_m' \widecheck{\mathbf{J}}_m ,\quad
\widehat{\mathbf{G}}_{t,m} := \widehat{\mathbf{Q}}_m' \widecheck{\mathbf{Y}}_{G,t}^{(m)} \widehat{\mathbf{J}}_m .
\]
Then for every $t\in[T]$, $\widehat{\mathbf{G}}_{t,m}$ satisfies that
\begin{align*}
    &\;\quad
    \Big\| \widehat{\mathbf{G}}_{t,m} - \mathbf{H}_{Q,m}' \widecheck{\mathbf{G}}_{t,m} \mathbf{H}_{J,m}
    \Big\|_F^2
    \notag \\
    &=
    O_P\Bigg(
    \min(p_m,q_m)
    + p_m^{\delta_{r,1}^{(m)}}
    q_m^{\delta_{c,1}^{(m)}}
    \big( \Delta_{R,m} + \Delta_{C,m} + \Delta_{F,m} \big)
    + \big( \eta_{Q,m} + \eta_{J,m} \big) p_m q_m
    \Bigg),
\end{align*}
where $\Delta_{R,m}$, $\Delta_{C,m}$, $\Delta_{F,m}$, $\eta_{Q,m}$, and $\eta_{J,m}$ are defined in the statement of Theorem~\ref{thm:common_comp_global_local_init}.

For $\mathbf{H}_{Q,m}$, note that
\begin{align*}
    \mathbf{I}_{k_r} &= \widehat{\mathbf{Q}}_m' \widehat{\mathbf{Q}}_m
    = (\widehat{\mathbf{Q}}_m - \widecheck{\mathbf{Q}}_m \mathbf{H}_{Q,m})' \widehat{\mathbf{Q}}_m
    + \mathbf{H}_{Q,m}' \widecheck{\mathbf{Q}}_m' \widehat{\mathbf{Q}}_m \\
    &=
    (\widehat{\mathbf{Q}}_m - \widecheck{\mathbf{Q}}_m \mathbf{H}_{Q,m})' \widehat{\mathbf{Q}}_m
    + \mathbf{H}_{Q,m}' \widecheck{\mathbf{Q}}_m' (\widehat{\mathbf{Q}}_m - \widecheck{\mathbf{Q}}_m \mathbf{H}_{Q,m})
    + \mathbf{H}_{Q,m}' \widecheck{\mathbf{Q}}_m' \widecheck{\mathbf{Q}}_m \mathbf{H}_{Q,m} \\
    &=
    (\widehat{\mathbf{Q}}_m - \widecheck{\mathbf{Q}}_m \mathbf{H}_{Q,m})' \widehat{\mathbf{Q}}_m
    + \mathbf{H}_{Q,m}' \widecheck{\mathbf{Q}}_m' (\widehat{\mathbf{Q}}_m - \widecheck{\mathbf{Q}}_m \mathbf{H}_{Q,m}) \\
    &\;\quad
    + \mathbf{H}_{Q,m}' (\mathbf{Q}_m'\mathbf{Q}_m)^{-1/2} \mathbf{Q}_m'\mathbf{Q}_m (\mathbf{Q}_m'\mathbf{Q}_m)^{-1/2} \mathbf{H}_{Q,m} \\
    &=
    \mathbf{H}_{Q,m}' \mathbf{H}_{Q,m} + 
    O_P\left\{
R(T,d_{\text{fac},\star})^{1/2} \;
p_m^{ (\delta_{q,1}^{(m)} -\delta_{q,k_r}^{(m)})}
\left( \frac{  \max_{n\in[M] \setminus \{m\}} s_{J,n}^2 p_n^{\delta_{q,1}^{(n)}}}{\max_{n\in[M] \setminus\{m\}} s_{J,n}^2 p_n^{\delta_{q,k_r}^{(n)}}} \right)
\right\}  \\
    &=
    \mathbf{H}_{Q,m}' \mathbf{H}_{Q,m} 
    + O_P\big( \eta_{Q,m}^{1/2} \big),
\end{align*}
where the last equality used Lemma~\ref{lemma: common_comp_global_local_init},
and the $O_P(\cdot)$ bound is in terms of the Frobenius norm.
Analogous arguments hold for $\mathbf{H}_{J,m}$. This thus completes the proof of this lemma.
